#### A. Scope 
* All exported or imported goods, whether subject to duties and taxes or exempt from duties and taxes, shall be subject to customs declaration.

#### Key Points
* All goods, regardless of duty status, require customs declaration.
* The scope applies equally to exported and imported goods.

#### B. Definitions 
* A customs declaration is a single administrative document (SAD) used for all customs regimes for the release of goods (import, export, customs bonded warehouse, etc.). 
* A customs declaration registered in the automated customs system is the sole legally valid document that may be used as evidence that the goods have been imported into or exported from Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* SAD is the unified document for all customs regimes.
* Only registered declarations in ASYCUDA are legally valid as evidence of import/export.

#### C. Lodgement of Customs Declaration 
* The customs declaration shall be lodged at an authorized customs office as designated by the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
* The customs declaration may be lodged at a customs office prior to the arrival of goods, in accordance with the prevailing legal instruments. 
* For importation, the customs declaration shall be lodged at the customs office within three (3) days after the arrival of the goods, unless the goods are placed under customs temporary storage or under the customs transit procedure. 
* For exportation, the customs declaration shall be lodged at the customs office at the time the goods arrive, or may be lodged prior to the arrival of the goods in accordance with applicable procedures.

#### Key Points
* Declarations must be lodged at authorized customs offices.
* Import declarations have a 3-day deadline after goods arrival (unless in temporary storage or transit).
* Export declarations can be pre-lodged or submitted at the time of goods arrival.

#### D. Declarant 
* Exported or imported goods shall be declared by the owner of the goods or by a person authorized to complete customs formalities on behalf of the owner. 
* Authorized persons to complete customs formalities include: 
    * Persons authorized as customs brokers by Ministerial Decree of the Minister of Economy and Finance; or 
    * Persons who are not professional customs brokers may complete customs declarations for their own business. 
* Such persons may be authorized to complete customs clearance procedures for others, on a temporary basis and for certain specific operations, subject to authorization by the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

#### Key Points
* Goods can be declared by the owner or an authorized representative.
* Authorized customs brokers and non-professional persons may act as declarants if permitted.
* Temporary authorization for declarants requires Ministry approval.

#### E. Customs Declaration Form and Attachments 
* Customs declarations shall be made electronically. 
* Customs declarations are not required to be printed and submitted in paper form to the customs administration. 
* Supporting documents required to attached to the customs declaration include: commercial invoice, packing list, and transport documents. 
* Where necessary, import/export permits, licenses, authorizations, certificates of origin, insurance certificates, and other relevant documents shall be attached to the customs declaration in electronic form. 
* Supporting documents already uploaded and approved in the National Single Window system or the automated customs system are not required to be uploaded again. 
* During customs declaration processing, supporting documents are not required to be translated, except where necessary.

#### Key Points
* All declarations must be submitted electronically.
* Key supporting documents include commercial invoices, packing lists, and transport documents.
* Previously uploaded documents do not need to be resubmitted.
* Translation of documents is not required unless necessary.

#### F. Commodity Items 
* Where multiple commodity items are declared in a single customs declaration, each item shall be considered as a separate declaration item. 
* Each item must be declared separately and classified accurately in accordance with the prevailing Customs Tariff.

#### Key Points
* Each commodity item in a declaration is treated as a separate item.
* Accurate classification according to Customs Tariff is mandatory.

---

#### A. Responsibilities of the Declarant 
* The declarant shall have the following responsibilities: 
* 1. Lodgement of Customs Declaration 
* Complete customs declaration data, verify all information fields, and upload supporting documents in electronic form, then register the Single Administrative Document (SAD) in the Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA). 
* The declarant shall be prepared to be present during physical inspection of goods and to respond to any questions raised by customs officers, where necessary. 
* If amendment or cancellation of a customs declaration is required, the declarant shall contact customs officers via the query function. 
* In case of questions related to declaration preparation, the declarant may request assistance from the Help Desk. 
* If the customs declaration is assigned to the red channel, the declarant or goods owner shall contact customs scanning officers (where available) to conduct scanning and physical examination officers to conduct physical inspection, in accordance with applicable legal instruments. 
* After final assessment, the declarant, goods owner, or authorized representative may pay duties, taxes, and/or other fees through the following options: 
    * Electronic payment (E-Payment): select “E-PAYMENT” in Section B of the customs declaration, then proceed with electronic payment through partner banks; 
    * Bank transfer or deposit: select “BANK TRANSFER” in Section B of the customs declaration, then transfer funds (Bank Transfer or KHQR) or deposit cash directly into the revenue account of the customs office. 
    * After payment, upload proof of payment (Transaction Details or Bank Slip) into ASYCUDA; 
    * Pre-payment account: enter the declarant’s bank account number in Box 48 of the customs declaration. 
    * Upon authorization, the system will automatically deduct payment if sufficient balance is available; 
    * Cash payment: select “CASH” in Section B, then pay cash to the customs cashier for system confirmation; or 
    * Other payment methods: proceed in accordance with prevailing legal instruments. 
* After payment of duties and taxes, electronic receipts and release notes will be automatically issued. 
* The declarant, for their personal use, may print them without requiring signatures or stamps from customs officers. 
* Refund receipts and vehicle document shall be collected from the cashier or accountant, without requiring signatures or stamps. 
* After customs release, the declarant shall request a cargo exit note in the system for stock control verification, then provide it to the driver in electronic (PDF) or paper form. 
* If a full or partial refund of paid duties and taxes is approved, the declarant or goods owner shall submit the original refund approval decision, customs declaration, customs receipt, and relevant documents to the customs accountant for verification and refund processing. 
* The declarant may track declaration status via the trader mobile application, customs website, or information boards at customs offices. 
* Release information shall be provided electronically. 
* The declarant may print paper copies of customs declarations for internal use and shall retain declarations and related documents in paper or electronic form in accordance with law. 
* The declarant shall not share account credentials with others. If ceasing permanent use of the account, it must be closed immediately. 
* Upon completion of operations, the declarant shall log out of the system and delete all files and empty the recycle bin when using public or customs office computers. 
* 2. Pre-Arrival Customs Declaration 
* After sufficient cargo declaration, the declarant may lodge a pre-arrival customs declaration (Pre-Lodged SAD) with supporting documents electronically. 
* Such declarations are subject to advance risk assessment and document review. 
* Examined pre-arrival declarations are not re-checked upon arrival unless amended or deemed high risk. 
* The declarant may amend or cancel pre-arrival declarations before customs review. 
* If goods do not arrive, cancellation must be requested with justification. 
* Upon arrival of goods, a pre-arrival customs declaration shall automatically be registered as a customs declaration and processed in accordance with prevailing procedures.

#### Key Points
* Declarants must complete all required fields and upload supporting documents electronically in ASYCUDA.
* Physical inspections require declarant presence and cooperation with customs officers.
* Pre-arrival declarations can be lodged electronically for advance risk assessment and document review.
* Pre-arrival declarations are not re-examined upon arrival unless they are amended or flagged as high risk.
* Declarants must maintain account security and log out after each session.

#### B. Responsibilities of Documentary Check Officers 
* Customs documentary check officers shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Verify completeness of customs declarations or pre-arrival declarations and supporting documents, confirm duties and taxes, and instruct ASYCUDA to conduct risk assessment and assign control channels. 
* Review selection criteria explaining channel assignment. 
* Verify cargo declaration information against the customs declaration. 
* Examine data accuracy against supporting documents: 
    * Detailed examination for yellow or red channel declarations; or 
    * Scrutinize examination for green or blue channel declarations. 
* The documentary check shall be conducted to the whole document without stopping at the first detected error. 
* Pre-arrival declarations already examined shall not be re-examined upon arrival unless amendments occur. 
* Record examination results in the Selectivity Control Page, including error codes and remarks in the Inspection Act where discrepancies are found.

#### Key Points
* Documentary check officers verify completeness and accuracy of declarations and supporting documents.
* Risk assessment and control channel assignment are conducted through ASYCUDA selectivity criteria.
* Yellow or red channel declarations receive detailed examination; green or blue channels receive scrutiny examination.
* Pre-arrival declarations already examined are not re-examined upon arrival unless amendments occur.

#### C. Responsibilities of Scanning Examiners 
* Customs scanning examiners shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Conduct scanning operations in accordance with legal instruments. 
* Analyze and assess scanned images against declared information. 
* Record scan analysis results in the system, indicating any suspicion and areas for physical inspection. 
* Red channel pre-arrival declarations may be scanned immediately upon arrival.

#### Key Points
* Scanning examiners verify declared information against scanned images.
* Analysis results are recorded in the system with indicators for areas requiring physical inspection.
* Red channel pre-arrival declarations are scanned immediately upon arrival.

#### D. Responsibilities of Physical Examiners 
* Customs physical examiners shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Receive schedule appointments with declarants for physical inspection. 
* Conduct physical inspection for red channel declarations with at least two customs officers present, in the presence of the declarant or goods owner. 
* Upon finishing the physical examination, whether or not discrepancies found, record inspection results in the Selectivity Control Page or mobile inspection application. 
* Where irregularities are found, conduct the followings: 
    * Conduct full inspection in according with the prevailing laws and regulations; 
    * Record findings in the Inspection Act, providing fraud codes, additional information, and remarks; and 
    * Prepare customs offence reports in accordance with prevailing laws and regulations. 
    * In this case, additional supporting documents may be required, and the customs declarations and attachments shall be printed into paper form as necessary. 
* Physical inspection may be conducted upon request or instruction, in according with the prevailing laws and regulations 
* During inspection, customs may take samples in accordance with legal instruments. 
* The samples goods are not subject to a separate customs declaration.

#### Key Points
* Physical inspections for red channel declarations require at least two customs officers present.
* Declarants must be present during physical inspection of their goods.
* Inspection results are recorded even if no discrepancies are found.
* Samples taken during inspection do not require separate customs declarations.

#### E. Responsibilities of Customs Query Officers 
* Customs query officers shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Meet with the declarant to hear explanations, make further inquiries regarding discrepancies, discuss amendments to the customs declaration, and may request additional relevant documents in electronic or paper form. 
* If agreement is reached with the declarant, the customs declaration found to contain actual errors shall be amended, and the rationale for such amendment shall be recorded in the Inspection Act. 
* If the customs declaration cannot be amended, it shall be cancelled in the system upon the declarant’s request. 
* In cases where the declarant provides sufficient acceptable evidence proving correctness, the customs declaration shall not be amended; 
* however, a response explaining such outcome must still be recorded in the Inspection Act. 
* If no agreement is reached with the declarant on amendment based on applicable laws and regulations, or if additional information is not provided, the reasons for disagreement shall be recorded in the Inspection Act in order to enable further action. 
* At the end of each working day, query customs officers shall manage and monitor declarations that remain pending customs clearance and report daily to the head of unit in order to urge declarants to expedite completion of their procedures, and shall prepare monthly reports as required.

#### Key Points
* Query officers meet with declarants to resolve discrepancies and discuss amendments.
* Amendments are made only if the declarant provides acceptable evidence or reaches agreement.
* Cancelled declarations require justification recorded in the Inspection Act.
* Query officers prepare daily and monthly status reports on pending clearances.

#### F. Responsibilities of the Chief Examiners 
* The Chief Examiners shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Review reports on examination results and rationales submitted by customs officers of all sections in the system, ensuring that operations comply with selectivity criteria and that examination results are adequate. 
* After receiving sufficient examination results, the Chief Examiner shall proceed as follows: 
    * Where examination results indicate no irregularities: 
        * For customs declarations, re-route the declaration to the green channel and instruct the ASYCUDA system to conduct final assessment; or 
        * For pre-arrival customs declarations initially assigned to green, blue, or yellow channels, re-route them to the green channel to await arrival of goods and final assessment. 
    * Where document examination reveals irregularities, the customs declaration or pre-arrival customs declaration shall be re-routed to query officers, with additional remarks provided where necessary. 
    * After amendments or feedback from query officers are deemed appropriate, declarations in green, blue, or yellow channels shall be re-routed to green and final assessment conducted. 
    * Red channel declarations shall await physical inspection results. 
    * Where physical inspection reveals discrepancies, the declaration shall await the customs offence determination decision, after which it shall be forwarded to query officers for amendment in accordance with the decision. 
* Where specific risk information is identified by customs officers, the Chief Examiner may re-route declarations to the yellow or red channel. 
* Where a decision is made to normalize or refund customs duties and taxes, the Chief Examiner may forward the declaration to query officers for normalization. 
* Where amendments are made to cargo declarations, pre-arrival declarations, customs declarations, or other adjustments, and such amendments present high risk, the Chief Examiner may re-route the declaration for re-examination by document examination officers and/or physical examination officers. 
* After arrival of goods, if examination results in ASYCUDA are sufficient and no irregularities are detected, the system shall automatically re-route the declaration to the green channel and conduct final assessment after sixty (60) minutes.

#### Key Points
* Chief Examiners review examination reports to ensure compliance with selectivity criteria.
* Declarations with no irregularities are re-routed to green channel for final assessment.
* High-risk or problematic declarations are re-routed for additional examination or query officer review.
* Red channel declarations await physical inspection results before final assessment.

#### G. Responsibilities of Customs Cashiers 
* Customs cashiers shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Generate payment advice for customs declarations that have completed final assessment, informing declarants of payable duties, taxes, and fees. 
* Upon payment of duties, taxes, and charges, customs cashiers shall: 
    * For electronic payments: verify transactions completed through electronic systems; 
    * For payments by transfer or deposit: verify transactions and generate payment receipts in the ASYCUDA system; 
    * For prepayment accounts: verify completed transactions; 
    * For cash payments: verify and receive cash from declarants and generate payment receipts in ASYCUDA; or 
    * For other payment methods: proceed with applicable laws and regulations. 
* Payment receipts are not required to be printed, signed, or stamped by customs officers. 
* Where full or partial refunds of paid duties, taxes, and charges are approved in accordance with laws and regulations, required documents including the original legal decision, customs declaration, payment receipt, and/or other relevant documents shall be referenced to process the refund. 
* A refund receipt shall be generated in ASYCUDA and printed in two (2) copies for the declarant’s acknowledgment. 
* One copy shall be retained with the customs officer and one copy provided to the declarant. 
* Where additional duties, taxes, or charges are required, additional payments shall be received and an “Other Payment” receipt generated in ASYCUDA. 
* If a refund is subsequently approved for such additional payment, an “Other Refund” receipt shall be issued in ASYCUDA. 
* At the end of each cashier shift, a provisional accounting report “Accounting by Payment Method” shall be printed to reconcile total amounts received by electronic payment, cash, bank instruments, and other credit instruments against payment records. 
* The provisional accounting report and totals of collected revenue and cleared declarations shall be submitted to customs accountants. 
* Any discrepancies shall be reported with an adjustment report. 
* Each customs and excise unit shall display its revenue account number at the information counter.

#### Key Points
* Cashiers generate payment advice and process duties, taxes, and fees through multiple payment methods.
* Payment receipts are automatically generated in ASYCUDA without requiring officer signatures or stamps.
* Refunds are processed with proper documentation and dual-copy receipt generation.
* Daily reconciliation reports are prepared to verify collected revenue and cleared declarations.

#### H. Responsibilities of Customs Accountants 
* Customs accountants shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Prepare daily accounting reports, including reports by transaction type, payment method, budget account, and other required accounting reports. 
* Review daily reports from authorized partner banks and record transactions in customs accounts. 
* Reconcile daily bank reports with bank slips provided by cashiers and report discrepancies to the unit head for further action. 
* At the end of each month, print monthly accounting reports by transaction type, payment method, budget account, and other required reports. 
* For vehicles subject to vehicle document, generate the vehicle document in ASYCUDA, print one (1) copy, and provide it to the declarant without requiring signature or stamp.

#### Key Points
* Accountants prepare daily and monthly accounting reports by transaction type and payment method.
* Daily bank reports are reconciled with customs accounts and discrepancies reported to unit heads.
* Vehicle documents are generated in ASYCUDA and provided without officer signatures or stamps.

#### I. Responsibilities of Customs Exit Note Officers 
* Customs exit note officers shall manage goods that have completed payment of duties and taxes but have not yet exited customs control area as follows: 
* Unless otherwise specified, goods authorized for exit shall require a cargo exit note, even if goods under a single declaration are transported by one means of transport. 
* Each exit note is valid for one-time use from origin to destination and does not require signature or stamp. 
* Exit notes may be generated by declarants or customs stock management officers: 
    * Where drafted by the declarant, officers shall verify exit note data against the actual means of transport; or 
    * Where no prior draft is made, officers shall create the exit note. 
* Approved exit notes shall be provided to declarants electronically. Upon request, paper copies may be printed without signature or stamp. 
* Manage, monitor, and compile balance records of cleared goods pending exit and prepare monthly balance reports as required.

#### Key Points
* Exit notes are valid for one-time use and do not require customs signatures or stamps.
* Declarants or customs officers can generate exit notes in the system.
* Cleared goods pending exit are monitored and monthly balance reports are prepared.

#### J. Responsibilities of Exit Gate Officers 
* Customs exit gate officers shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Verify transportation exiting storage locations such as ports, dry ports, warehouses, or other authorized locations: 
    * At locations equipped with customs-controlled electronic gate systems, exit verification shall be automated; or 
    * At other locations, exit verification shall be conducted by customs officers. 
* Where irregularities are detected, report to the head of unit for further action.

#### Key Points
* Exit verification is automated at locations with electronic gate systems.
* Manual verification is conducted at other locations by customs officers.
* Irregularities detected during exit verification are reported to unit heads.

#### K. Responsibilities of Help Desk Officers 
* Customs help desk officers shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Facilitate and guide goods owners or authorized representatives in preparing and lodging customs declarations upon request. 
* Provide advice to traders and the public on customs procedures and other information as feasible. 
* Each customs and excise unit shall display an updated list of Help Desk officers at the information counter.

#### Key Points
* Help Desk officers facilitate and guide goods owners in preparing and lodging customs declarations.
* They provide advice on customs procedures to traders and the public.
* Contact information is posted at information counters for public access.

#### L. Responsibilities of Management of Customs Clearance Unit 
* Heads of customs clearance units shall have the following responsibilities: 
* Bear full responsibility for cargo declaration and customs clearance operations within their units. 
* Organize, assign, or adjust staffing by function to ensure operational efficiency and continuity, including requesting creation, modification, or deletion of system user accounts. 
* Monitor daily declaration status reports from query officers and urge declarants to expedite completion of procedures. 
* Oversee all operations and processes, provide guidance as necessary, and take immediate corrective action in accordance with applicable laws and regulations where irregularities are detected.

#### Key Points
* Unit managers bear full responsibility for cargo declaration and clearance operations.
* They organize staffing by function to ensure operational efficiency and continuity.
* They monitor daily declaration status and encourage timely completion of procedures.
* They oversee all operations and take corrective action when irregularities are detected.

#### M. Responsibilities of Post-Clearance Audit Officers 
* Customs officers may conduct post-clearance audits on customs declarations and related documents stored in the ASYCUDA system and may print such documents as necessary.

#### Key Points
* Post-clearance audits are conducted on declarations and related documents in ASYCUDA.
* Officers can print necessary documents for audit purposes.

#### Related Legal Instruments: 
* Ministerial Decree No. 1447 MEF.BRK dated 26 December 2007 on Provision and Procedure of Customs Declaration 
* Ministerial Decree No. 788 MEF.BRK.GDCE dated 27 October 2023 on Pre-Arrival Processing Procedures 
* Ministerial Decree No. 924 MEF.BRK.GDCE dated 12 December 2023 on Amendment of the Principles and Procedures for the Identification of Export-Import Goods and Transit Goods, Loaded in Containers Subject to Inspection through the Scanning System 
* Instruction No. 4353 GDCE dated 13 July 2023 on Detailed Procedures and Responsibilities for Electronic Cargo Declaration and Customs Declaration Process

#### Key Points
* Goods must be reported to Customs before unloading from conveyances.
* Imported goods can be for home use, temporary import, or duty-suspended condition.
* Goods can be removed from clearance areas and placed in temporary storage or bonded warehouses under customs control.
* Temporarily imported goods must be re-exported and remain under customs control.

#### Reporting of goods entering Customs territory: 
* All goods, equipment and conveyance that are imported into the Customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia must without delay be transported through legal routes to the nearest Customs office or to another place designated by Customs, and be declared to Customs in accordance with the requirements. 
* The requirements to declare the goods to Customs 
    * shall be applied equally regardless the country of origin or the country of export 
    * shall be fulfilled through a summary Customs declaration when the goods enter Customs territory 
    * any person who declares the goods to Customs shall be responsible for the accuracy of the declaration. 
    * goods are to be reported at an authorized Customs office. 
    * persons who wish to declare goods to Customs at locations other than at a customs office must first obtain written authorization from Customs. 
    * persons who wish to declare goods to Customs outside the hours of operation of the Customs office must obtain prior authorization from the Customs. 
    * persons who is responsible for declaring goods to Customs must make the goods and the conveyance available for inspection by customs when requested, and must answer truthfully any questions, asked by customs.

#### Key Points
* All goods and conveyances must be transported through legal routes to authorized Customs offices.
* Declaration requirements apply equally regardless of country of origin or export.
* Goods must be available for inspection and declarants must answer questions truthfully.
* Prior authorization is required to declare goods outside authorized locations or office hours.

#### Submission of Goods Manifest to Customs: 
* Goods arriving by sea or other water ways shall be recorded on the vessel manifest or general cargo list that is to be carried onboard the vessel. 
* These documents must be signed by the captain and must contain the detail information of the goods and the place where the goods were loaded on the vessel. 
* Prohibited goods shall be reported on the manifest with their true description, by nature and type. 
* It is prohibited to report as a single item on a manifest of several items packaged individually, even if they are parts of a consolidated shipment.

#### Key Points
* Sea freight goods must be recorded on vessel manifests or general cargo lists.
* Manifests must be signed by the captain and contain detailed goods information and loading locations.
* Prohibited goods must be reported with true descriptions by nature and type.
* Individual items cannot be reported as a single manifest item.

#### The Submission of Relevant Transportation Documents to Customs: 
* When a vessel arrives Customs territory, requested by Customs, the captain shall provide documents as follows: 
    * Original Manifest to Customs officers who have authority to issue visa that states “No Amendment”. 
    * A set of Cargo Manifest and other related documents to Customs. 
* Within 24 hours after the arrival, the captain shall show and provide Customs documents as follows: 
    * Vessel’s report 
    * Cargo Manifest (Considered as summary declaration) 
    * Bill of Lading 
    * Special Manifest for Warehouse in the vessel, Crew List and List of Crew Personal Effect 
    * Vessel rental contract 
    * Vessel Registration Certificate and other documents that are required by Customs administration to implement Customs measures. 
* At the request of Customs Administration, manifest shall be provided to customs administration before arrival of the vessel. 
* Manifest can be provided to customs through electronic forms if available.

#### Key Points
* Captains must provide original manifests within 24 hours of vessel arrival.
* All required transportation documents must be submitted within 24 hours.
* Manifests must be pre-submitted to Customs on request before vessel arrival.
* Electronic manifest submission is permitted when available.

#### Moving Goods from Vessel: 
* Moving goods from vessel can only be done in the premises of port where Customs office locates. 
* The movement or transfer of goods from the vessel shall be authorized in writing by the Customs Administration, and with the presence of Customs officers. 
* The movement and transfer of goods from the vessel shall be done in the working hours of the Customs Office and under the terms set by the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
* The equipment for use in the vessel, which received tax and duty exemption, shall be kept in block secured with seal if necessary and be presented to Customs officers if required until the vessel departs.

#### Key Points
* Goods can only be moved from vessels in port premises where Customs offices are located.
* Written authorization from Customs is required for goods movement.
* Movement must occur during Customs office working hours.
* Vessel equipment with tax/duty exemption must be kept secured with seals until departure.

### Placing goods in Customs Temporary Storage: 
* Goods that are placed in Customs Temporary Storage is subjected to inspection by Customs and must be compliant with existing procedures. 
* Goods are placed in Customs Temporary Storage for reasons as follows: 
    * waiting for necessary documents for completing Customs formalities 
    * waiting for transferring or separating from the containers 
    * for goods inspection 
    * waiting for customs clearance and to pay taxes and duties. 
* Goods that are placed Customs Temporary storage shall be released immediately after submitting Customs declaration in order for release the goods or for transit, and after completing Customs clearance. 
* According to Customs clearance procedures, payment of tax, duty, fee, and requirements of submitting Customs declaration and necessary documents shall be suspended for goods placed in Customs Temporary Storage. 
* All goods can be placed into Customs Temporary Storage except: 
    * prohibited goods for export and import 
    * goods that can be dangerous to people and to other goods, or are required to have separate storage with special equipment to store. 
* Maximum duration of Customs Temporary Storage is forty-five days (45 days) from registered date on Customs declaration for Customs Temporary Storage which locates outside the airports. 
* Over the above duration, goods shall be placed in Customs warehouse automatically if there is no customs declaration. 
* During the period when the goods are in Customs warehouse, the owner of goods shall pay customs storage fee: 0.1% of customs valuation per day to the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
* This fee shall be noted on Customs declaration and paid into state’s budget. 
* Within three months from registered date on the list of Customs warehouse, all goods that are not fulfilled with Customs declaration in Customs Temporary Storage shall be considered as unclaimed goods, and imposed under Articles 54 and 55 of the Customs Law.

#### Key Points
* Customs Temporary Storage is for goods awaiting documents, clearance, or inspections.
* Maximum storage duration is 45 days outside airports and 30 days at airports.
* Storage fees are 0.1% of customs valuation per day after the duration limit.
* Goods not cleared within three months are considered unclaimed and subject to auction or other disposal.

#### Required documents to attach to SAD for Customs clearance: 
* Invoice and packing list 
* Manifest 
* Bill of lading 
* Permit or License or Certificate (if required), and 
* Other related documents 
* The import via Customs offices of ports, excluding Phnom Penh International Port and Sihanouk Ville International Port, has to be registered in monitoring list of goods and conveyances by port with attached documents listed in point 6 above. 
* If the captain of any vessel does not provide the manifest or other similar related documents, Customs officers do not allow to unload goods into Customs warehouse (Customs Temporary Storage) or Common Control Area. 
* Regarding the Customs clearance process and tax payment for import goods by port (sea/rivers), please read articles of Customs Declaration Provisions and Procedures via Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA), and of Prakas on Import and Export Tax and Duty Payment Procedures.

#### Key Points
* Required documents for port import include invoices, packing lists, manifests, bills of lading, and permits.
* Customs offices other than Phnom Penh and Sihanouk Ville ports must register goods in monitoring lists.
* Vessels without proper documentation cannot unload goods into customs warehouses.

#### Declaration of Goods Imported into Customs Territory by Air: 
* Aircrafts departing and arriving Cambodia must notify the State Secretariat of Civil Aviation of the Kingdom of Cambodia. 
* All air-cargo has to be listed in the manifest signed by the flight captain. 
* The manifest has to be organized the same as that of point 3 (port) above. 
* The captain has to provide the manifest and other related documents to Customs immediately. 
* The captain has to keep these documents as summary declaration at Customs office of airports, when the aircraft arrives. 
* Unloading cargo along the runway is prohibited. However, the captain has the right to unload objects including balancing object, documents, and cargo to secure the aircraft. 
* Unloading and transferring cargo are implemented the same as that of transport by sea or river, stated in point 4 above. 
* When flying in Cambodia’s airspace, aircrafts are not allowed to unload goods at location other than the designated route; 
* except it may eventually lead to danger which is to be reported to the nearest Customs office where the aircraft will land. 
* Loading and unloading cargo and passengers’ baggage into and out of the aircraft must be under the control and inspection of Customs officers. 
* When Customs officers inspect the aircraft, pilots or representatives have to ensure smooth cooperation. 
* If the aircraft is in danger or to avoid danger by landing at any airports without presence of Customs officers, pilots or representatives have to inform the local authority there to conduct inspection on behalf of the Customs officers.

#### Key Points
* Aircraft must notify State Secretariat of Civil Aviation upon departure and arrival.
* Air cargo must be listed in manifests signed by the flight captain.
* Cargo loading and unloading must be under Customs control and inspection.
* Unloading cargo along runways is prohibited except for safety-critical items.

#### Storing Cargo in Customs Temporary Storage: 
* The period of storing cargo in Customs Temporary Storage at airports from date of registering Customs declaration is 30 days. 
* When the above storing period is over, the goods shall be automatically placed in Customs warehouse if the cargo is not declared to Customs. 
* During the period when goods is in Customs warehouse, the owner must pay customs storage fee of 0.1% per day of CIF value. 
* The fee is recorded in Customs Declaration and transferred into the state’s budget. 
* Over 3 months from arrival date, goods, which are not removed from the Customs Temporary Storage, shall be considered as unclaimed goods,and placed under article 54 and 55 of the Law on Customs.

#### Key Points
* Maximum air cargo storage period is 30 days from Customs declaration registration.
* Storage fees are 0.1% per day of CIF value after duration limits.
* Goods not cleared within three months become unclaimed and subject to disposal.

#### Required documents to attach to SAD for Customs clearance: 
* Invoice and packing list 
* Manifest 
* Airway Bill 
* Permit or License or Certificate (if required), and 
* Other related documents 
* Regarding the Customs clearance process and tax and duty payment, please read articles of Customs Declaration Provisions and Procedures via Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA), and of Prakas on Import and Export Tax and Duty Payment Procedures.

#### Key Points
* Required air import documents include invoices, packing lists, manifests, airway bills, and permits.
* Air cargo storage limit is 30 days; after which goods are placed in customs warehouse.
* Standard Customs clearance procedures apply to air imports.

#### Declaration to Customs Authority: 
* When goods arrive at land-border in Customs territory of Cambodia, importer or representative must declare the goods and conveyance to the Customs authority as stated in the Law on Customs, and Prakas on the Declaration of Goods Arriving in the Customs Territory of Kingdom of Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* Land-border goods must be declared to Customs authorities upon arrival.
* Declarations must comply with Customs Law and related Prakas regulations.

**Import good originated in neighboring countries:** 
* Import goods is recorded daily in a monitoring list of arriving goods and conveyance crossing land border by clearly indicating its final destination including international transit, national transit to a domestic dry port, or outside a dry port or Special Economic Zone (SEZ). 
* Fulfilment of Customs procedure (at border area) must be done in a dry port or Common Control Area managed by Customs at the border area, except import goods in small quantity which is to be implemented according to the existing laws (Circular No. 007 MEF dated December 29th, 2009 on the management of import and export goods in small quantity).

**Imported goods from non-neighboring country:** 
* The goods must be recorded daily to track the arrival of the goods, and the conveyance​​​ and specify the final destination of the goods such as international transit, national transit to special economic zone or any dry port in the country. 
* The goods originated in a non-neighboring country imported via port using neighboring countries’ ports and transit via land transport to Cambodia must undergo these specific procedures: 
    * must be stored in containers when transit to Cambodia unless specifically authorized by the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia (GDCE). 
    * can only be imported and processed at some international land border checkpoints determined by the GDCE. 
    * must be placed and complete the Customs formalities only in dry ports or Common Control Area at the border area managed by Customs, except for goods under international transit or transit to dry ports or Special Economic Zones specified by the GDCE. 
    * If the declaration of goods is not in the red channel, the competent Customs officer must re-route to the red channel which is subjected to physical inspection in accordance with the existing procedures. 
* Supporting documents to the Customs declaration is the same as those of goods imported through international ports, especially the Bill of Lading (B/L).

#### Key Points
* Goods from neighboring countries are recorded in monitoring lists with clear final destinations.
*Goods from non-neighboring countries imported via neighboring country ports must be containerized and processed at designated checkpoints.
* Non-neighboring country goods may be re-routed to red channel for mandatory physical inspection.

#### Documents to be submitted with Customs declaration: 
* Invoice and Packing List 
* Cargo Manifest 
* Bill of Lading 
* Track Waybill 
* Permits or licenses or certificate (in case required) 
* Other related documents 
* Further detail related to Customs clearance and duty and tax payment on goods imported by land can be found in our articles on of Customs Declaration Provisions and Procedures via Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA), and of Prakas on Import and Export Tax and Duty Payment Procedures.

#### Key Points
* Required land import documents include invoices, packing lists, cargo manifests, bills of lading, and track waybills.
* All documentation must be submitted with the Customs declaration.
* Standard Customs clearance and duty procedures apply to land imports.

* Exported goods are to be reported at a customs office or a place designated by the Customs. 
* Exported goods either obliged to export duty or exempted from duty are subject to Customs declaration.

#### Key Points
* Exported goods must be reported at authorized Customs offices or designated locations.
* All exports are subject to Customs declarations regardless of duty status.

#### The necessary attached documents are: 
* Invoice and packing list 
* Bill of lading / Airway Bill, Trucking bill of lading 
* Permit issued by the customs (except the exportation by Qualified Investment Projects or rice exportation) 
* Permit or certificate or license from other governmental authorities (if required)

#### Key Points
* Export documents include invoices, packing lists, bills of lading/airway bills, and trucking bills of lading.
* Customs permits are required except for qualified investments or rice exportation.
* Additional permits or licenses from other authorities may be required.

#### Customs Procedure for Exportation: 
* In accordance with the existing regulations, the exportation by port (sea/rivers), land, and air shall follow procedures below: 
    * For non-containerized goods, the exporter or his representative shall: 
        * Directly make a request to Customs office​​ or branch 
        * After getting the approval, the exporter or his representative shall make an export declaration in accordance with the Prakas on the Provision and Procedure of Customs Declaration with the aforementioned attachment. 
    * For non-prohibited containerized goods, the exporter or his representative shall fulfill the customs formalities at the Department of Export Management of the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
    * For goods in the list of prohibited and restricted goods, the exporter or his representative shall obtain an export permit from relevant ministries/authorities in accordance with Sub-Decree on Implementation of the List of Prohibited and Restricted Goods, and fulfill the existing customs formalities. 
    * The containerized exported goods may be subject to the requirement to go through scanning machine. 
    * (Please refer to the information about Scanning Containerized Goods)

#### Key Points
* Non-containerized goods require approval before export declaration filing.
* Containerized goods are processed at Department of Export Management.
* Prohibited/restricted goods require export permits from relevant authorities.
* Containerized exports may require scanning machine inspection.

#### Key Points
* Outside customs office formalities are available for hazardous, explosive, or inflammable goods.
* Agricultural and forest product exports can be cleared outside customs offices.
* Qualified investment firms can export containerized cargo using outside customs office procedures.

#### Procedure on Exportation of Rice and Agricultural Products: 
* Rice exportation has been provided the priority to skip the queue with the highest facilitation of customs clearance in accordance with laws and regulations in force, and is exempted from customs processing fee. 
* For exportation of agricultural products, the exporter or representative can request to conduct customs clearance outside the customs offices. 
* For containerized agricultural products, exporter or representative can request permit and conduct export customs clearance at Department of Export Management, or at exit offices which the officers of Department of Export Management are there.

#### Key Points
* Rice exports receive priority queue status and highest facilitation with no processing fees.
* Agricultural products can request outside customs office clearance.
* Containerized agricultural products are cleared at Department of Export Management or designated exit offices.

* Customs Transit is a customs procedure that allows goods to be transported from one customs office to another under customs supervision. 
* Goods and means of transport under transit are not subject to the payment of duties and taxes;  however, they may be subject to other charges related to the transit operation.

#### Key Points
* Customs Transit allows goods to be transported between customs offices under supervision.
* Goods in transit are not subject to import duties or taxes.
* Other charges related to transit operations may apply.

## Types of Customs Transit 
* **International Transit** refers to the transportation of goods from a customs office of entry, into the customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia, and onward to a border customs office of exit, out of the customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia. 
* **National Transit** refers to the transportation of goods: 
    * From a border customs office of entry to an inland customs office or an authorized location within the customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia; 
    * From an inland customs office or an authorized location to a customs office of exit; or 
    * From an inland customs office or an authorized location to another inland customs office or another authorized location.

#### Key Points
* International Transit moves goods from entry to exit across the Cambodia customs territory.
* National Transit moves goods from border to inland location, within inland locations, or to exit.

### A. Scope 
* This Instruction applies to national transit (import) and international transit of goods. 
* For international transit operations, transit operators may apply customs transit procedures in accordance with international agreements to which the Kingdom of Cambodia is a signatory.

#### Key Points
* General provisions apply to both national and international transit.
* International transit procedures follow applicable international agreements.

### B. Persons Eligible as Customs Transit Operators 
* Persons eligible as customs transit operators include: 
    * Customs Temporary Storage operators; 
    * Customs Bonded Warehouse operators; or 
    * Other persons who have obtained prior authorization from the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* Eligible transit operators include customs storage and bonded warehouse operators.
* Other persons can become operators with prior GDCE authorization.

### C. Guarantee 
* Guarantees for customs transit operations shall be lodged with the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia through the Accounting Office of the Department of Finance and Personnel. 
* For a single transit operation, the declarant may request to lodge the guarantee at the customs office of departure. 
* The minimum guarantee amount shall be equivalent to the suspended duties and taxes for the customs transit operation, unless otherwise authorized by the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
* Guarantee procedures shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

#### Key Points
* Guarantees cover suspended duties and taxes for transit operations.
* Minimum guarantee amount equals suspended duties/taxes unless otherwise authorized.
* Single operation guarantees can be lodged at the customs office of departure.

#### Key Points
* Permitted transit containers must be sealable, durable, and designed for repeated use.
* Containers must be capable of being sealed by customs without tampering.
* Bulk goods can use unsealed vehicles if goods are clearly identified by examination or seals.
* Officers monitor goods to prevent alteration, removal, or addition during transit.

### E. Goods Prohibited from Transit 
* Goods fall under absolute prohibition under applicable laws and regulations; 
* Goods prohibited from transit under international agreements; or 
* Other goods as determined by the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* Absolutely prohibited goods under applicable laws cannot be transited.
* Goods prohibited by international agreements are restricted from transit.
* GDCE can determine additional goods prohibited from transit.

## II. Customs Transit Procedures

### A. Obligations of the Transit Operator 
* The transit operator or its representative shall have the following obligations:

#### 1. Application for Customs Transit Authorization 
* An application for customs transit shall be submitted by completing the required data in accordance with Annex “C” of this Instruction and attaching the necessary supporting documents, such as bill of ladings, invoices, packing lists, permits (if required), and other relevant documents, in electronic form, and shall be implemented as follows: 
    * For customs transit into a Special Economic Zone, the application shall be submitted to the Customs and Excise Office stationed at the Special Economic Zone. 
    * For other customs transit cases, the application shall be submitted to the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia through the Department of Customs Regimes. 
* Authorized Economic Operators and Best Traders are not required to submit a prior application. 
* The transit operator may apply for customs transit authorization prior to the arrival of the goods. 
* The transit operator shall monitor responses, requests for amendment, and/or requests to attach additional supporting documents as required by competent customs and excise officers. 
* In case of amendment, extension of validity, or cancellation of an approved transit application, the transit operator or its representative shall submit a request for amendment, extension, or cancellation to the authority that reviewed and approved the original transit application.

#### Key Points
* Transit applications must include supporting documents in electronic form.
* SEZ transits are submitted to SEZ Customs offices; others to GDCE via Department of Customs Regimes.
* AEO and Best Traders are exempt from prior application requirements.
* Pre-arrival applications are permitted; amendments require officer approval.

#### 2. Customs Office of Departure 
* For customs transit to a Special Economic Zone within a radius of 20 (twenty) kilometers from the border checkpoints, the transit operator or its representative shall present the approved transit authorization to the competent customs and excise officers at the customs office of departure, without being required to lodge a transit declaration. 
* For customs transit other than the above case, the transit operator or its representative shall lodge a transit declaration and pay applicable fees (if any). 
* Documents attached at the time of applying for transit authorization are not required to be reattached to the transit declaration. 
* The transit declaration and supporting documents are not required to be printed in paper form for submission, nor are they subject to return the paper back to the customs office of departure. 
* The transit declaration may be lodged prior to the arrival of the goods, in accordance with existing pre-arrival processing procedures, and advance payment of fees is permitted. 
* If amendment or cancellation of the transit declaration is required, the transit operator or its representative shall submit a request for amendment or cancellation through the customs officer responsible for reviewing transit documentation. 
* Where goods are required to undergo scanning and/or physical inspection, the transit operator or its representative shall contact the customs officer responsible for scanning inspection and/or the customs officer responsible for physical inspection in order to comply with applicable customs procedures. 
* After approval of the transit declaration, a payment advise shall be automatically generated, and the transit operator or its representative shall pay the fees as stated in the payment advise. 
* After payment, the transit operator or its representative may download the electronic payment receipt, without requiring signature or stamp from customs officers. 
* The transit operator or its representative shall request a customs transit accompany document (TAD) in the system and provide it to the driver to accompany the means of transport, in electronic (PDF) or paper form. 
* One TAD shall be valid for only one means of transport and one transport journey.

#### Key Points
* SEZ transits within 20km of border need only authorization, not declaration.
* Transit declarations require lodging and fee payment except for SEZ near borders.
* Pre-arrival declarations and advance payment are permitted.
* TAD must be obtained and provided to drivers; each TAD is single-use only.

#### 3. En-routing 
* The transit operator or its representative shall be responsible for the customs transit en-routing operation as follows: 
    * The goods under customs transit shall be transported from the customs office of departure to the customs office of destination in compliance with the prescribed arrival time and the legally designated route. 
    * No unloading, substitution, additional loading of goods, or damage to customs seals shall be permitted. 
    * Where it is necessary to change the means of transport or the transport route, the operator shall submit a request through the system. 
    * In the event of an accident resulting in partial or total loss or damage to customs seals or goods, the operator shall not remove the goods from the means of transport without authorization from customs officers, except where the safety of the goods or public safety is threatened, and shall immediately contact the nearest competent customs and excise officers and provide notification through the system.

#### Key Points
* Goods must follow prescribed arrival times and legally designated routes.
* No unloading, substitution, or additional loading is permitted during transit.
* Route changes require operator request submission through the system.
* Accidents require immediate notification to nearest customs office without removing goods.

#### 4. Customs Office of Destination 
* For national transit, after authorization for the means of transport to depart has been granted, the declarant may lodge an import customs declaration prior to the arrival of the goods at the customs office of destination. 
* The transit operator or its representative shall present the TAD, the means of transport, and the goods to the competent customs and excise officers at the customs office of destination. 
* The transit operator or its representative shall participate in the physical inspection at the customs office of destination, where required.

#### Key Points
* National transit allows pre-arrival import declarations at customs office of destination.
* TAD, transport, and goods must be presented to customs officers at destination.
* Operators must participate in physical inspections when required.

#### 1. Obligations of Verify Officers 
* Verify officer of transit applications shall have the following obligations: 
    * Verify the completeness, accuracy, and consistency of data and supporting documents submitted by the transit operator or its representative. 
    * Where necessary, request the transit operator or its representative to attach additional supporting documents. 
    * Where irregularities are detected, return the application to the transit operator or its representative, specifying the indicators requiring amendment or completion. 
    * Where the application cannot be amended or supplemented, it may be rejected with specific reasons stated in the system. 
    * Where no irregularities are detected, forward the application to the Reviewing Officers.

#### Key Points
* Verify officers check completeness, accuracy, and consistency of applications and documents.
* Additional supporting documents may be requested when necessary.
* Applications with irregularities are returned for amendment or rejected with reasons.
* Approved applications are forwarded to Reviewing Officers.

#### 2. Obligations of Reviewing Officers 
* Reviewing officers of transit applications shall have the following obligations: 
    * Examine the submitted transit application to ensure that it is accurate and compliant with applicable laws and regulations. 
    * Where irregularities are detected, return the application to the transit operator or its representative, specifying the indicators requiring amendment or completion. 
    * Where amendment or supplementation is not possible, the application may be rejected with specific reasons. 
    * Where no irregularities are detected, forward the application to the competent management level for approval and, where necessary, provide comments to the management level.

#### Key Points
* Reviewing officers examine applications for legal and regulatory compliance.
* Problematic applications are returned to operators for amendment or rejected.
* Approved applications are forwarded to management level for final approval.
* Comments on applications are provided when necessary.

#### 3. Obligations of the Approving Officers 
* The management level responsible for approving transit applications shall have the following obligations: 
    * Review and approve transit applications in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. 
    * Where necessary, require the lodging of a guarantee for customs transit applications. 
    * Where it is deemed that a transit application cannot be approved, reject the application with stated reasons for rejection.

#### Key Points
* Management level reviews and approves applications per applicable laws.
* Guarantees for transit operations can be required when necessary.
* Rejected applications must include stated reasons for rejection.

#### 1. Obligations of Customs Officers Reviewing Transit Documents 
* Customs officers reviewing transit documents shall have the following obligations: 
    * Customs transit into a Special Economic Zone within a radius of 20 (twenty) kilometers from the border checkpoints that does not require lodging a transit declaration, shall not be subject to document inspection at the customs office of departure. 
    * For other customs transit cases, the following shall apply: 
        * Verify the completeness and accuracy of the transit declaration, the goods declaration, and the declared fees. 
        * Where irregularities are detected, notify the transit operator or its representative for clarification and may provide information on indicators requiring amendment. 
        * Upon completion of document inspection, record the inspection results in the system, whether compliant or non-compliant, and may provide comments for customs officers responsible for scanning inspection and/or physical inspection. 
    * At the end of each operational day, manage and monitor customs transit transport operations that have not yet arrived at the destination. 
    * Where expired cases are identified, contact the transit operator to clarify the reasons and report to the head of the unit. 
    * Contact relevant competent customs and excise officers and take appropriate measures in case of notifications as stipulated in Point II.A.3(4) above.

#### Key Points
* SEZ transits within 20km of borders do not require document inspection at departure.
* Transit declaration, goods declaration, and fees must be verified for completeness.
* Document inspection results are recorded and communicated to scanning/physical inspection officers.
* Expired transit operations are monitored and transit operators contacted for explanation.

#### 2. Obligations of Customs Officers Responsible for Physical Inspection at the Customs Office of Departure 
* Customs officers responsible for physical inspection shall have the following obligations: 
    * Verify the TAD provided by the transit operator or its representative or generate a TAD upon request by the transport operator or its representative, verify consistency with the actual means of transport and container, and affix customs seals to the container and/or means of transport. 
    * If information in the system is found to be inconsistent with the means of transport, customs seals, or other information, make the necessary corrections prior to authorizing departure of the means of transport. 
    * Where electronic customs seals are used, comply with applicable procedures for the use of electronic seals. 
    * Where goods are subject to physical inspection based on instructions or high-risk indicators, conduct the inspection with the participation of at least two customs officers and in the presence of the transit operator or its representative. 
    * Where a customs offense is detected, prepare a customs offense report in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

#### Key Points
* TAD verification must match actual transport and container information.
* System corrections are made before authorizing transport departure.
* Electronic customs seals must comply with applicable procedures.
* Physical inspections require at least two officers and transit operator presence.
* Customs offense reports are prepared when offenses are detected.

#### 3. Obligations of Customs Cashier Officers 
* Customs cashier officers shall have the following obligations: 
    * When payment of duties, taxes, and all types of fees is made, customs cashier officers shall proceed as follows: 
        * Electronic payment: conduct post-verification of transactions paid through the electronic system. 
        * Payment by transfer or deposit: verify the completed payment transaction and generate a payment receipt in the system. 
        * Cash payment: verify and receive cash from the declarant and generate a payment receipt in the system. 
        * Other forms of payment: comply with applicable laws and regulations. 
    * Upon request, customs cashier officers shall print and provide the payment receipt to the transit operator or its representative without requiring signature or stamp. 
    * Where refund of guarantees or fees is authorized, implementation shall be in accordance with applicable regulations.

#### Key Points
* Payment processing includes electronic, transfer/deposit, cash, and other approved methods.
* Payment receipts are provided without signature or stamp requirements.
* Guarantee and fee refunds are processed per applicable regulations.

### D. Obligations of Customs Officers at the Customs Office of Destination 
* Customs officers at the customs office of destination shall have the following obligations: 
    1. Upon arrival of the means of transport, immediately confirm in the system that the customs transit transport has arrived. 
    2. Where the goods arrive after the prescribed date and time, inquire into the reasons for the delay. 
    3. Where the reasons are unjustified or the delay exceeds 3 (three) days, prepare a report to the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia for review and appropriate action on a case-by-case basis. 
    4. Examine the integrity of customs seals and the arriving means of transport and detach the customs seals. 
    5. Where there is suspicion or other risk indicators, conduct physical inspection at the customs office of destination and record the inspection results in the system. 
    6. Prepare a customs offense report in accordance with applicable procedures where irregularities in customs seals, means of transport, or goods are detected that constitute violations of the Law on Customs or other applicable regulations. 
    7. At the end of each operational day, manage and monitor customs transit transport operations that have not yet arrived at the destination. 
    8. Where expired cases are identified, contact the transit operator to clarify the reasons and report to the head of the unit. 
    9. Contact relevant competent customs and excise officers and take appropriate measures in case of notifications as stipulated in Point II.A.3(4) above.

#### Key Points
* Arrival confirmation in system is immediate upon means of transport arrival.
* Delays beyond 3 days require report submission to GDCE for case-by-case action.
* Customs seal integrity is examined and seals detached at destination.
* Physical inspections are conducted when suspicion or risk indicators exist.
* Customs offense reports are prepared for irregularities constituting violations.
* Expired transit operations are monitored with transit operator contact and unit head reporting.

### A. Authorized Consignees 
* Authorized consignees include: 
    * Authorized Economic Operators (AEO); or 
    * Other persons who have obtained prior authorization from the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* Authorized Economic Operators (AEO) can use simplified transit procedures.
* Other persons require prior GDCE authorization to use simplified procedures.

### B. Benefits and Responsibilities 
* Authorized consignees are entitled to the following benefits and responsibilities in the customs transit process: 
    * Authorized to use special seals that have been pre-approved by the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
    * Authorized to complete customs transit formalities at their own business premises without being required to present the goods at the supervising customs office of departure. 
* In such cases, the transit operator or representative shall comply with the following: 
    * Upon arrival of the goods at the premises, the authorized consignee shall notify the system of the arrival of the means of transport and the goods. 
    * If there is no response from, or authorization is granted by, the customs and excise authority managing simplified transit procedures, the authorized consignee may detach the seal and complete the customs transit formalities on their own. 
    * In the event of any irregularities, they shall immediately report to the customs and excise authority managing simplified transit procedures without delay. 
    * If the authorized consignee receives a response from the customs and excise authority managing simplified transit procedures indicating that self-completion of customs transit formalities is not permitted, they shall wait for the presence of competent customs and excise officers to remove the seal and complete the customs transit formalities. 
* Authorized consignees shall be responsible for any irregularities arising during their customs transit operations, in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

#### Key Points
* Authorized consignees can use pre-approved special seals.
* Authorized consignees can complete transit formalities at their own premises.
* Self-detach of seals is permitted if no response or authorization is received.
* Irregularities must be immediately reported to customs authorities.
* Authorized consignees are liable for irregularities during transit operations.

### C. Responsibilities of Customs Control Office Managing Simplified Transit Procedures 
* The customs control office managing simplified transit procedures shall have the following responsibilities: 
    * Review authorized transit operations prior to arrival at the premises and respond to the authorized consignee regarding approval for self-detach of seals or the requirement for the presence of customs officers. 
    * In cases where the presence of customs officers is required to detach seals and/or conduct physical inspections, at least two customs and excise officers shall be assigned to complete customs formalities at the authorized consignee’s premises.

* Scanning containers is a mechanism of trade facilitation which allows Customs authority to strengthen effectiveness of physical inspection of goods conveyed in containers by spending short period of time, and decreasing unnecessary expenses for unloading goods for the inspection.

## I. Containerized Goods to Pass through Scanning Machines 
* All import-export goods conveyed in a container which is subjected to pass inspection by scanning machines or inspection system of TC-Scan are as follow: 
    * The SAD is in red channel assessed by the ASYCUDA 
    * The SAD is in other channels, but subjected to be rerouted into red channel according to risk information identified by the Customs officers 
    * At Customs clearance office, the goods’ owner requests that the goods are to be inspected by a scanning machine 
    * Other condition determined by the Customs Administration.

## II. Containerized Goods Not to Pass through Scanning Machine: 
* Containerized import-export goods, which is subjected to exemption of passing scanning machine or inspection system, TC-Scan, are as follow: 
    * Export goods which was inspected before loading into the container, and secured with seals by the competent Customs officers. 
    * Import-export goods loaded into a container without roof or walls 
    * Import-export goods to be fulfilled Customs clearance at Customs and Excise offices at the border, which are not equipped with scanning machine 
    * Import-export goods of the government institutions, diplomat or organizations with diplomatic immunity, International Organizations, or NGOs which are officially authorized by the competent authorities 
    * Import-export goods which are humanitarian aid or donation 
    * Goods authorized by the Ministry of Economy and Finance to be exempted from this obligation 
    * Goods imported by members of Best Trader group in accordance with the principles of Customs risk management 
    * Empty containers, and 
    * Other goods determined by the GDCE

#### Key Points
* Pre-inspected and sealed export goods are exempt from scanning requirement.
* Open-top containers and goods at border offices without scanners are exempted.
* Diplomatic immunity and humanitarian goods receive exemption from scanning.
* Ministry of Economy and Finance can authorize additional exemptions.
* Best Trader members receive scanning exemptions per risk management principles.

## III. Containerized Goods Requested to Be Transported under National Transit Procedure: 
* Dry port operators may choose a place for goods to be scanned either at sea/river check-points or at a Dry Port Customs and Excise Office which is equipped with a scanning machine. 
* Scanning of transit goods to Special Economic Zone is exempted.

#### Key Points
* Dry port operators select scanning location at sea/river checkpoints or dry ports.
* Scanning locations must be equipped with operational scanning machines.
* Special Economic Zone transit goods are exempt from scanning requirements.

#### Key Points
* Dry port operators can choose scanning locations at border checkpoints or dry port offices.
* Transit goods to Special Economic Zones are exempt from scanning requirements.

## IV. Scanning Fee Payment 
* Scanning fee of must be paid as follows: 
    * 64,000 (sixty-four thousand) Riel for a container with size over 40 feet 
    * 40,000 (forty thousand) Riel for a container with size less than 40 feet. 
* Particularly, scanning fee is reduced for containers of exported rice, which passes scanning machine as follows: 
    * 16 (sixteen) USD for a container with size over 40 feet 
    * 10 (ten) USD for a container with size less than 40 feet. 
* Note: 
    * To facilitate export, related traders may directly pay the scanning fee at Customs clearance offices for the export goods which is passed inspection system of scanning machine.

#### Key Points
* Scanning fees: 64,000 Riel for containers over 40 feet; 40,000 Riel for smaller containers.
* Rice exports receive reduced scanning fees: 16 USD (over 40 feet) and 10 USD (smaller containers).
* Traders can directly pay scanning fees at clearance offices for export goods.

## Best Traders 
* The incentive schemes offered to high compliant traders, known as the Best Trader Incentive Mechanism (BTIM), is a program that is part of a broader trade facilitation policy of the Royal Government of Cambodia. 
* This program first came into effect on 23rd June 2014 at the certification ceremony for the members of the Best Traders Group at the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia. 
* As of April 2021, 43 companies have been recognized by the GDCE as member of the Best Traders Group. 
* As a way forward, the GDCE is considering selecting more companies to become part of this program with the view to fully implement the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) program as stipulated in the Strategy for Customs Reforms and Modernization (SCRM) 2019-2023.

#### Key Points
* Best Trader Incentive Mechanism (BTIM) is a trade facilitation program for high-compliant traders.
* Program launched in June 2014; as of April 2021, 43 companies are members.
* GDCE plans to expand the program and implement full AEO program by 2023.

#### Key Points
* Applicants must rank 1st in TCMS with minimum 1 billion KHR capital.
* No serious customs offences or unpaid customs debts in past 3 years.
* Proper recordkeeping and business community membership are required.
* Minimum 2 million USD annual trade volume is mandatory.

### Incentive Package 
Members of the Best Traders Group are eligible to a number of facilitative treatments such as: 
* Prioritized queuing during the time of declaration lodgment, documentary check, physical inspection, payment, and other procedures without having to follow first-in first-out principle 
* Documents deferment without having to submit the guarantee of 20% of the value of the goods imported provided that the goods are: 
    * Not listed under the prohibited and restricted list of goods stipulated in the existing regulation or 
    * Listed under the prohibited and restricted list of goods stipulated in the existing regulation under the condition that the goods have been authorized for importation by relevant authority. 
* Exemption of advance verification of customs valuation and certificate of origin 
* For Qualified Investment Project (QIP), traders can request for customs import permit directly at the customs office of importation, and the stock management can be self-managed. 
* Such traders are required to carry out stock management with the Department of Customs Procedures at the GDCE only once at the end of every month. 
* Exemption from having to carry with the goods transport permit and the requirement to have customs seal posted on goods upon the arrival at business premise 
* Pre-arrival clearance procedure 
* Destination clearance at customs bonded warehouse and temporary storage premise with national transit request carried out at the office of entrance without having to obtain permission from the GDCE 
* Eligibility to lodge export declaration at the closest customs and excise office and having the lodgment processed and consignment inspected by officers of the said office at the trader’s premise except cases not permitted by risk 
* Exemption from the requirement to obtain advance permission from the GDCE for re-exportation or re-importation procedure.

#### Key Points
* Best Traders receive prioritized queuing and document deferment privileges.
* QIP traders can self-manage stock with monthly reporting to GDCE.
* Exemptions from transport permits, seals, and advance permissions are granted.
* Pre-arrival and destination clearance procedures provide additional trade facilitation.

### Best Trader Membership Application 
Qualified traders wishing to become a member of the Best Traders Groups shall submit the application to the GDCE with the following documents attached: 
* Certificate of Business Registration and Company’s Bylaw and list of shareholders as of the date of application 
* Financial Statement for the last two years (if required)

* VAT Certificate and/or Patent Certificate or similar certificate

* Term and Document Checklist 01 Copy

* Letter of Authorization for company’s representative 01 Copy 
* List of authorized employees 01 Copy 
* Cambodian National ID
