* According to the Law on Investment of the Kingdom of Cambodia, Only Qualified Investment Projects are entitled to the benefits subject to the scope of this Law. 
* Qualified Investment Project, abbreviated to “QIP”, is the investment project which has received a Final Registration Certificate. 
* To be admitted as a QIP, the investor has to register the investment project with the Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC) or Provincial-Municipal Investment Sub-Committee (PMIS) and receive a Final Registration Certificate (FRC). 
* There are three types of Qualified Investment Project: 1) Domestically Oriented Qualified Investment Project, 2) Export Oriented Qualified Investment Project, and 3) Supporting Industry Qualified Investment Project.

#### Key Points
* QIP receive exemption of customs duties and taxes based on their investment classification.
* Domestic, Export-Oriented, and Supporting Industry QIP have different duty exemption levels.
* Production inputs used for export are subject to quarterly review and retrospective duty assessment.

#### Exemption of Customs Duties 
Conforming to the Sub-Decree No. 111 on the Implementation of the law on the Amendment to the Law on Investment of the Kingdom of Cambodia, a QIP shall be entitled to the exemption based on each category of QIP as follows: 
* **Domestic Oriented QIP** refers to a QIP that does not aim at export. 
    * Production Equipment and Construction Materials imported by a Domestic QIP are exempt from Customs Duties. 
    * In the case where the QIP has a capability to directly export any portion of its manufactured products or has supplied for export industry, the quantity of Production Inputs that were taxed at the time of import and later used to produce goods directly or indirectly exported shall be entitled to customs duties exemption after a review of the quarterly report. 
* **Export Oriented QIP** refers to a QIP that sells or transfers a proportion of its product to a purchaser or transferee outside the Kingdom of Cambodia. 
    * Production Equipment, Construction Materials, and Production Inputs imported by Export QIP are exempt from customs duties. 
    * However, for the QIP which operates under the customs bounded warehouse mechanism, the customs duties exemption shall be in compliance with the law and regulations in force applicable to the mechanism. 
    * The processed Production Inputs that have not been exported shall be subject to the payment of customs duties and Taxes applicable at the time of import after review of the quarterly report. 
* **Supporting Industry QIP** refers to a QIP that supplies 100% percent of its products to export QIP instead of imported raw materials and accessories. 
    * Production Equipment, Construction Materials, and Production Inputs imported by a Supporting Industry QIP are exempt from customs duties. 
    * However, in the case where the QIP failed to supply 100% of its manufactured products to the export industry or directly export its products, then the quantity of the QIP’s production inputs used to produce those goods shall be subject to the customs duties and taxes after review of the quarterly report.

#### Key Points
* VAT and special taxes on imported production inputs are borne by the Royal Government.
* Exemptions apply to garment, textile, footwear, and supporting industries.
* Supporting industry QIPs receive exemptions for inputs directly supplied to export manufacturers.

* **For Export Garment Industry:** 
    * Value Added Tax on imported production inputs is born by the Royal Government (Circular No.110 dated January 27, 1999 on Implementation of VAT on inputs imported by Export Garment Factories). 
    * Special Tax on imported production inputs for Garment Industry is borne by the Royal Government (Letter No. 393 GDCE dated March 26, 2015 of GDCE). 
* **For Other Export Industries:** 
    * Special Tax on imported production inputs of other Export Industries is borne by the Royal Government (Letter No. 758 GDCE dated June 04, 2015). 
* **For Supporting Industry QIP for Export Industry:** 
    * VAT on imported production inputs and production equipment to directly supply for Garment Industry, Textile Industry, Footwear Industry, Carry-Bag and Handbag Industry and Hat Industry is borne by the Royal Government (Prakas No. 311. MEF.BK dated March 19, 2014 of Ministry of Economy and Finance). 
    * Special Tax on imported production inputs for Supporting Industry is born by the Royal Government (Letter No. 393 GDCE dated March 26, 2015 and Letter No. 758 GDCE dated June 04, 2015 of GDCE).

#### Key Points
* QIP must obtain Master List approval from CDC before importing duty-exempted goods.
* Customs Permit must include invoices, packing lists, and transportation documents.
* QIP follow standard customs declaration procedures after obtaining Customs Permit.

In order to import Production Equipment, Construction Materials, or Production Inputs with the exemption of customs duties or taxes, QIP shall fulfill following conditions: 
1. Investors or their representatives shall apply for Master List of imported goods from the Council for the Development of Cambodia (Cambodian Investment Board-CIB). 
2. After getting approval from CDC or CIB, the above master list shall be submitted to GDCE (Department of Customs Procedure) or National Single Window 
3. When goods in the above master list are imported, investors or their representatives shall apply for Customs Permit through National Single Window, attaching with supporting documents such as invoices, packing lists, transportation document, authorized letters, and other related documents if necessary. 
4. After obtaining Customs Permit, investors or their representatives shall complete the procedure of Customs Declaration as the procedure in force.

#### Key Points
* Department of Export Management conducts customs formalities at temporary storages and QIP manufacturing premises.
* Customs officers seal containers after physical inspection on the right side of door.
* Seals are removed by customs officers at exit offices after accuracy verification.

#### General Procedures for Export Customs Clearance 
* Department of Export Management, assisted to the GDCE, has functions and duties for assigning monitor teams and inspect teams to manage, operate, control, and collect tax, duty, and other fees and do customs formalities according to current regulations at customs temporary storages, and/or manufacturing premises of QIP, on exported goods under QIP as determined by GDCE (Article 61 of Prakas 147 MEF dated 08 February 2018). 
* Investors are able to request customs officers to do export formality at their manufacturing premises, or consolidate with the others into the same container at customs temporary storage. 
* After physical inspection, customs officer seal on the right side of container door. 
* Customs seal will be removed after customs officers at exit offices check for the accuracy.

#### Customs clearance procedures 
* All exporters shall attach relevant documents to process customs clearance as in the procedure of customs declaration.

#### Key Points
* SEZ procedures vary based on distance from official checkpoints (within/beyond 20km).
* Investors may unload goods without customs officer presence under risk management policy.
* Master List verification ensures goods match approved import classifications.

##### A. For SEZ located near the official checkpoint or within twenty (20) kilometers from inland or coastal border of Customs Zone 
* Competent customs officer to SEZ shall consider and propose to GDCE for determining the seamless route and appropriate period to transport goods in-out between SEZ and official checkpoint.

**Procedures at Official Checkpoint** 
* Importers only show and provide competent customs officer at official checkpoint a copy of documents related to goods for transit to SEZ without submitting Customs Declaration. 
* The documents shall include invoice/packing list, transport documents or other documents mentioned the information of goods for transit to SEZ located nearby the official checkpoint.

**Procedures at SEZ** 
* The investors shall submit documents related to goods for transit which are mentioned above to the competent customs officer. 
* The competent customs officer shall preliminarily verify the identification of involved individual, means of transport and related documents and then allow the goods to enter the investor premises or other Areas of SEZ in case Investors do not have a proper place to store their goods. 
* The importers can unload their goods for using or processing according to their need without the presence of Customs officer in accordance with a policy of Trade Facilitation through Risk Management, except for a special request from those officers who have permission from the representative of GDCE to SEZ. 
* Once the goods have been unloaded, importers shall submit Customs declaration by clearly describe each item whether or not being stated in the master list approved by SEZ Administration or Cambodian Special Economic Zone Board. 
* The competent customs officer shall manage to verify all items declared above with Master List. 
* Investor can request to the representative of GDCE to SEZ for advance clearance importation of goods which are not in the Master List but are under incentive scheme in accordance with Sub-Decree No. 148 ANKr.BK above. 
* Other Items which are not under incentive scheme are subject to implementation of normal customs procedures especially related to duties and taxes and other restrictions.

**1. Requesting for Customs Transit** 
* The Investors shall submit written request to customs at official checkpoint for transportation of goods under national transit procedure from official checkpoint to designated SEZ. 
* This written request for transportation of goods under national transit procedure shall be endorsed by competent customs to SEZ. 
* For best traders, the written request is not required to be endorsed by competent customs to SEZ.

**2. Customs officers to SEZ** 
* Customs officers to SEZ shall endorse (to certify that mentioned investors are located in designated SEZ) on the application for transportation of goods under national transit procedure within two (2) working hours in case the required documents are accurate and sufficient according to existing regulations.

**3. Customs officers at official checkpoint** 
* Customs officers shall provide the priority in examining and verifying the request and urgently allow the transportation of goods to SEZ by just fixing customs bullet seal and attached with transit documents on means of transport in accordance with Customs Transit procedure in force. 
* In case the transportation cannot be fixed with customs bullet seal such as non-containerized goods, customs officers at checkpoint shall arrange surveillance mechanism.

**4. Customs officers to SEZ** 
* When transit goods arrive at SEZ, Customs officer shall implement the procedures mentioned in point A.2 at SEZ above.

#### Key Points
* SEZ investors lodge export declarations at SEZ; customs officers verify and seal containers.
* Direct exports receive priority examination without queueing at official checkpoints.
* Risk management policy may permit physical inspection only with written permission from office head.

##### A. Direct Export from SEZ

**1. Investors** 
* Investors lodge export customs declaration at SEZ in accordance with existing procedures.

**2. Customs officers to SEZ** 
* Customs officers to SEZ verify export customs declaration 
* If there is no irregularity, competent customs officers shall urgently release goods in order to transport to office of exit by just fixing customs bullet seal and attached with export documents on means of transportation. 
* In case of non-containerized cargo, customs shall arrange surveillance mechanism.

**3. Customs officer at official checkpoint** 
* Competent Customs officers shall urgently examine regularity of the means of transportation and related documents without queueing. 
* In case there is no irregularity, customs officers urgently remove customs bullet seal and urgently release goods for export. 
* Customs officers can conduct physical inspection in case there is exact irregularity and written permission from head of customs office of official checkpoint in accordance with policy of trade facilitation through risk management.

##### B. Export from SEZ via Dry Port 
* Letter No. 653 GDCE dated 02 August 2011 on facilitation of Customs procedures for transporting goods out of Special Economic Zone to dry ports to consolidate into the container with other goods to be exported to foreign countries.

**1. Investors** 
* Investors submit the application form (3 copies) to competent customs officers to SEZ requesting to transport goods to dry port.

**2. Customs officers to SEZ** 
* Customs officers to SEZ shall endorse and give permission to transport goods out of the zone by just fixing customs bullet seal and attached with related documents on means of transportation.

**3. Customs officers of Department of Export Management** 
* When goods arrive at dry port, owner or representative of the goods shall urgently inform competent customs officers of Department of Export Management to verify the regularity of seal and means of transportation and certify the arrival of goods. 
* In case there is no irregularity, competent customs officer remove seal and immediately permit the fulfillment of export customs formalities or unloading the goods to warehouse under the responsibility of dry port operator for future Customs formalities, waiting for completion of export customs formalities in accordance with customs procedures in force. 
* When finishing export Customs formalities, Customs officers inspect goods and permit loading the goods into the container and fix bullet seal.

#### Key Points
* Goods diverted to domestic market must undergo same import formalities as standard imports.
* Investors must obtain Zone Administration approval for goods with quality issues or out-of-date status.
* All diverted goods are subject to full import duties and taxes.

#### A. Approval from Zone Administration 
* With regard to the sale into domestic market of the production outputs which are not of proper quality, inferior quality or out-of-date goods and that cannot be exported, the Investors shall request for approval from Zone Administration.

#### B. Customs Procedures 
* All goods which are diverted to domestic market, in whatever conditions, shall be required to fulfill the same formalities as goods imported into the Kingdom of Cambodia and shall be subject to import duties and taxes by lodging Customs declaration according to customs procedure in force.

#### Key Points
* Temporary admission permits importing goods conditionally relieved from duties and taxes.
* Imported goods must be re-exported within one year; extension possible with justification.
* Machinery and specialized equipment taxed at reduced rate (20% annually or 2% monthly).

* Temporary admission means the customs procedures under which certain goods can be brought into the customs territory conditionally relieved in total or in part from payment of duties and taxes. 
* Those goods are to be imported for a specified purpose, and are to be re-exported within a specified period without having undergone any change except normal depreciation due to the use of them (Article 9 Law on Customs).

### Goods to Be Authorized to Import under Temporary Admission
* Importation of goods under the temporary admission may be authorized under the following cases:
    * Goods for display or use at exhibitions, meetings or similar events with reasonable quantity.
    * Professional equipment necessary for a technician or professional person entering Cambodia to perform a specialized task or job. The mentioned equipment does not include machineries and specialized equipment used in the manufacturing industry, packaging of goods, for exploitation of natural resources, construction or improvement of buildings, land development or similar projects.
    * Containers, pallets, packages, samples and other goods, imported in connection with a commercial transaction, but which are not goods purchased or sold in any part of the commercial transaction.
    * Goods imported exclusively for educational, scientific or cultural purposes, including parts for scientific equipment and educational material which is authorized to import under temporary admission.
    * Goods, imported for sports purposes, which are used by tourists, athletes, business travelers for competition or demonstrations or for training within the customs territory.
    * Other materials used for promoting tourism and attracting tourists to visit the country.
    * Goods imported by passengers travelling across border for their own use.
    * Goods imported for humanitarian purposes including laboratory and surgical equipment and goods used to relieve victims of natural disasters and similar catastrophes.
    * Transport means conveying persons and goods for commercial use such as vessels, aircrafts, road vehicles, or trains which are used for international transportation whether or not for fare payment, including spare parts, accessories and equipment.

### Conditions for Temporary Admission
* To import goods under temporary admission procedure, the following conditions shall be fulfilled:
    1. Has to submit a request for authorization from GDCE (Department of Customs Procedure) prior to the importation.
    2. The application must clearly state the type of goods, quantity, value, purpose, goods owner, duration of the temporary admission and date of re-exportation.
    3. Imported goods under temporary admission are subject to lodgment of customs declaration and security.
* The security could be cancelled or returned upon having the confirmation of re-exportation.
* Machineries and specialized equipment used in the manufacturing industry, packaging of goods, for exploitation of natural resources, construction or improvement of buildings, land development or similar projects may be authorized by Customs to import under temporary admission for a specified period. 
* Obligation of duties and taxes on these goods are levied at the reduced rate of 20% of the duties and taxes according to customs tariff in force, for each year. 
* In case the period of import under temporary admission less than one year, the obligation of duties and taxes shall be calculated for each month at the rate of two percent (2%) of the total duties and taxes of those goods.
* Imported goods under temporary admission procedure shall be re-exported within one year from the date of importation. 
* This period could be extended by customs administration if written request, with the reasonable purpose, is submitted before expiry date.

#### Key Points
* Duties and taxes are suspended while goods are stored in bonded warehouses.
* Three bonded warehouse types exist: Public Type A, Private Type B, and Special Type C warehouses.
* Goods can be stored for up to 2 years with possible 12-month extension.

* A customs bonded warehouse is a building, place or an area that is authorized to store goods for a specified period of time under the customs control. 
* Import goods and domestic goods destined for export may be placed in a customs bonded warehouse. 
* While goods are stored in a customs bonded warehouse duties and taxes are suspended. 
* Any restrictions and prohibitions on the goods may be waived up to the time the goods are released for home use, or exported.

#### Key Points
* Type A public warehouses serve any person with legal goods rights.
* Type B private warehouses are authorized exclusively for specific operators and duty-free shops.
* Type C special warehouses store hazardous goods or items requiring special facilities.

* There are three types of Customs bonded warehouse:
    * **Type A:** Public Bonded Warehouses are customs bonded warehouses that are authorized by Minister of Economy and Finance and may be operated by the government agencies or by any approved person. Any person who has the legal right to goods may store their goods in a Public Bonded Warehouse, including importers, and person to whom the goods have been sold while in the warehouse, or any other person having the legal right to dispose of the goods.
    * **Type B:** Private Bonded Warehouses are custom bonded warehouses that are authorized by the Director General of General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia and to be solely used by authorized persons for storage of specific goods for their own use, including operators of duty-free shops.
    * **Type C:** Special Bonded Warehouses are customs bonded warehouses that are authorized by the Director of Customs and that are used for the storage of hazardous goods, goods that could affect the quality of other goods, or goods that require special storage facilities. Such warehouse may be private or public.

#### Key Points
* Goods can be sold or transferred while in warehouse; ownership changes must be reported to customs.
* Goods transferred to other bonded warehouses require transfer documents authorization.
* Export goods are released without duties/taxes; home use goods charged according to tariff rates.

* Goods may be stored in the customs bonded warehouse for up to 2 years from the date of customs declaration registration. 
* Before its expiry date, owner of the goods may request for an extension for storage of goods of up to twelve (12) months if the goods are still in good condition.
* While stored in customs bonded warehouse, goods can be sold or transferred. The importer or owner of the goods shall inform customs in writing of this transfer of ownership.
* Goods stored in a customs bonded warehouse can be transferred to another licensed customs bonded warehouse under customs control. Transfer documents shall be submitted to customs for all such transfers.
* Goods removed for export shall be subject to lodgment of customs export declaration ; and no import or export duties and taxes shall be charged, except domestic goods which may be subject to export taxes.
* Applicable duties and taxes on goods removed for home use shall be charged according to the customs tariff and the rates of duties and taxes in effect on the date of registration of the customs declaration for removal of the goods from the bonded warehouse.
* Owner of the goods in customs bonded warehouses shall be allowed by customs to inspect goods, take samples and carry out necessary operations to preserve those goods given that those actions do not change the essential characteristics of the goods. 
* Those operations can be fumigating, drying, cleaning, testing, and normal handling operations such as breaking bulk, repackaging, sorting and grading, marking, labelling or tagging and so on.

#### Key Points
* Duty free shops are Type B bonded warehouses for selling goods to foreign travelers and diplomats.
* Monthly import quotas determined; imported goods subject to 10% fee.
* Transported goods require transportation permits; loaded trucks marked with company logo.

### About Duty Free Shop
* Duty Free Shop is a Type B of Customs-Bonded Warehouse that complied with existing laws and regulations and administered by the GDCE for selling imported goods to foreign travelers.
* Types of duty free shop:
    * International departure terminal duty free shops,
    * International arrival terminal duty free shops,
    * Downtown duty free shops, and
    * In-flight or on-cruise duty free shops.

#### Key Points
* Monthly import quotas set per Circulation No. 007 MEF; import permits required from GDCE.
* Imported goods subject to 10% fee; clearance and payment at entering gate.
* Duty free shops include international terminal, downtown, and in-flight/on-cruise stores.

* Quantities and items imported under duty free shop scheme are determined as monthly import quotas in according to the Annex of Circulation No. 007 MEF dated 25th July 2018.
* Every import shall be required the import permit issued by the GDCE (Department of Excise).
* Goods imported under duty free shop scheme are subject for 10% fee.
* Customs clearance and fee payment shall be done at the customs and excise branch or office at entering gate in according to existing laws and regulations.

### Transportation of Goods Imported under Duty Free Shop Scheme
* Every transport of goods imported under duty free shop scheme within the country shall be attached with transportation permit.
* In necessary case, at least two customs officers will escort the goods to destinations.
* Loading trucks shall be painted the company logo and affixed a transporting card, issued by the GDCE (Department of Excise), on the front mirror of the trucks.

### Selling Goods Imported under Duty Free Shop Scheme
* Customers of Duty free shop are foreign travelers, foreign​ crews, diplomats and other authorized persons by Ministry of Economy and Finance.
* Sales quota for each inbound customer shall be allowed in according to the Annex of Circulation No. 007 MEF dated 25th July.
* Sales for each outbound customer shall not be restricted; however, the customer shall bear own responsibility for any procedures and quantity restriction in destination countries.
* Downtown duty free shops are allowed to sell goods with unlimited amount to customers but the goods shall be handed-over and picked up at any border gates of the Kingdom of Cambodia under customs control, except the goods, in suitable quantity for a passenger or for personal use in accordance to existing regulations, that get particular approval from the MEF to hand-over the goods at the shops.
* Goods imported under duty free shop scheme shall be affixed sticker: “CAMBODIA DUTY NOT PAID”.

### Obligations of Duty Free Shop Operators
* Depositing 5% of total annual duties and taxes on goods in the warehouses as guarantee to the GDCE.
* Paying annual license fee at 1% of monthly average duties and taxes on goods in the warehouses or at least 2 million KHR.
* Fully obeying legal contract on establishment and operation of duty free shops and other related regulations.
* Completely supporting and cooperating with relevant competent officials.
* Reporting timely and keeping customer‘s data for customs audit.
* Fully taking legal responsibilities to the leakage of goods imported under duty free shop scheme into domestic market.

### Management of Goods with Exemption of Duties and Taxes
* Goods imported with exemption of import duties and taxes under subparagraph (a) of the first paragraph of Article 26 of Law on Customs for or by foreign diplomatic or consular missions, international organizations and agencies of technical co-operation of other governments, for using in the exercise of their official functions and their personnel uses shall be exported after completion of their missions.
* Such goods and others stated under the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 26 of Law on Customs are not allowed to sell, transfer, divert to other non-authorized uses, or disposed of without the prior authorization from the customs authorities.
* Organizations or persons, who wish to sell, transfer, divert to other non-authorized uses, or dispose of goods imported with fully or partially exempt from import duties and taxes shall request for prior permission from customs administration in accordance with following procedures:
    * Shall apply for customs permit to customs administration by clearly indicating of how destinations or ownership of goods have been changed.
    * A copy of this request shall be sent to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, or to the Cambodian Development Council (CDC) for the goods imported under the provisions of the first paragraph, Praka 1 of the Prakas No. 105 MEF dated 15 February 2008 on Management of Goods exempted from duties and taxes.
    * The request shall be attached with list of goods and import documents as well as other relevant documents.
* The goods are not allowed to sell, transfer, or divert prior to permission from customs administration.
* New owner is obliged to payment of duties and taxes to customs administration in accordance with customs procedures in force.
* Goods shall not be transferred to new owners without prior authorization from the customs administration and before paying of duties and taxes or being granted another exemption from the competent authorities.
* Customs shall consider the real condition and status of the goods when delivered, and possibly adjust customs value accordingly.
* Goods originated in the Customs territory or imported with duties and tax paid previously or that are returning from abroad, that have not been enhanced in value, shall be allowed to be sold, transferred, diverted to uses or disposed of without prior authorization of Customs.
* Organizations or persons who wish to dispose of goods imported with exemption of import duties and taxes, shall request for prior permission from Customs.
* The request shall be attached with items list and import documents as well as other relevant documents.
* Goods disposal may occur after the authorization from Customs. Customs may examine the disposal or destroying of such goods.

### Advance Ruling
* Advance Ruling has been established and implemented in Cambodia since 4th January 2013 in order to enhance trade facilitation and to ensure the accuracy of completion of customs declaration (SAD) according to the provision of Customs Law.
* Advance Ruling is a written statement issued by the GDCE to the requesting person.
* There are 3 types of Advance Rulings:
    * Advance Ruling on Tariff Classification 
    * Advance Ruling on Customs Value (generally, this ruling provides interpretation of the regulations related to the customs valuation; it is not for the purpose of advance verification or determination of customs value) 
    * Advance Ruling on Origin of the Goods 
* The Advance Ruling is considered as an official document and legally valid for three years from the effective date of the issuance.
* In order to get benefit from Advance Ruling, the importers shall attach a copy of the Advance Ruling to the SAD at the time of clearance.

#### Key Points
* Importers, goods producers, and authorized persons can request Advance Rulings.
* Three types available: Tariff Classification, Customs Value, and Origin of Goods.
* Rulings valid for 3 years; copy must be attached to SAD at clearance.

* an importer,
* a producer of the goods,
* or any person authorized to do importation Units in Charge of Advance Rulings

### Units in Charge of Advance Rulings
* Department of Planning and Technique of the GDCE is in charge of receiving the request and issuing an Advance Ruling, with the following subordinate offices:
    * Tariff Classification Office, in charge of the Advance Ruling on Tariff Classification 
    * Customs Valuation Office, in charge of the Advance Ruling on Customs Value 
    * Rules of Origin Office, in charge of the Advance Ruling on Origin of the Goods

### Procedure to request for an Advance Ruling
1. In order to request for an Advance Ruling, the applicant must have knowledge of the raised issues and complete all the information in Advance Ruling application form in Khmer or English and sign.
2. Request Forms of Advance Ruling are as below:
    * AR-TC Form 1 for Advance Ruling on Tariff Classification 
    * AR-CV Form 1 for Advance Ruling on Customs Value 
    * AR-OG Form 1 for Advance Ruling on Origin of Goods.
3. An Advance Ruling request can only be used for a single goods (one HS code), or a single import transaction.
4. The applicant must submit the request with necessary documents, in person, to the above offices in charge and pay public service fee in amount of 200,000 Riels per request.
5. In case, the applicant is authorized by the goods owner, the authorization letter must be attached.

**Necessary documents to be attached to the request:**
* A certified and stamped copy of the identification document of the requesting company and the applicant such as VAT Registration Certificate, Annual Patent, authorization letter, ID card, or passport, etc.
* A sample of goods with other supporting documents indicating specification of the goods such as catalogue, production formula, usage, composition of goods, production process, etc. (For Advance Ruling on Tariff Classification) 
* Buy-and-Sell documents and reference of importing transaction, for the requested goods, such as purchase order, a sale contract, a pro forma invoice or a letter of credit (L/C), etc. (For Advance Ruling on Customs Valuation)

### Processing request for an Advance Ruling
* The GDCE will write the applicant an Advance Ruling with a full explanation of the reasons for the ruling on tariff classification and origin of the goods within 30 working days, and the ruling on customs valuation within 90 working days, from the receipt of all necessary information.
* If all such information is not received with the application, additional information will be requested by a notice and the time standard of 30 working days does not include the waiting period for the additional information.
* In this regard, applicant will be given a period of 30 working days from the date of the notice (or longer period as the notice may provide) to supply additional information or to fulfill other requirements.
* If there is no response to the notice within the time allotted, the Advance Ruling’s request will be closed administratively and considered withdrawn.

### Conditions invalidating Advance Rulings before expiration:
* An Advance Ruling will be invalid before expiry date if some characteristics related to importing goods are different from that in the Advance Ruling, or the amendment of the existing laws, or regulations affect the Advance Ruling, or the GDCE provides decision on amendment or withdrawal of the Advance Ruling, or if it is amended after being reviewed.

### Request for Review of Advance Ruling
* The applicant may request for review of the issued Advance Ruling within 45 days after the date of issuance.
* To oppose the issued Advance Ruling, the GDCE requires that the applicant, in person, lodges review application with issued Advance Ruling and written reasons at the competent office.
* The review application form consists of:
    * AR-TC Form 4 for Advance Ruling on Tariff Classification 
    * AR-CV Form 4 for Advance Ruling on Customs Valuation 
    * AR-OG Form 4 for Advance Ruling on Origin of the goods 
* The request will be processed in accordance with procedure stipulated in Paragraph 1 of “Process of Advance Ruling Application”.
* After examining and evaluating, the competent office would decide on the application, and the decision may replace the reviewed Advance Ruling.

### Publication of Advance Rulings
* In order to ensure transparency, Advance Rulings, with some information unrelated to the applicant’s personal identity, may be publicly published via some media like internet.
* The applicant has to inform the GDCE about confidential information contained in the application or application for reviewing Advance Ruling to ensure that this information would not be publicly published.

#### Key Points
* Transaction Value (method 1) is primary valuation method, covering over 90% of trades.
* Six valuation methods exist in sequence; inapplicable methods can be skipped.
* Decentralization allows local customs offices to value goods, reducing clearance time.

* Customs value of imported goods is the value which is used as the basis for customs tax and duty calculation by multiplying this customs value with the rate of customs duty.
* Tax and duty calculated with this method is called Ad Valorem Duty.
* Importer or relevant individual must declare customs value in the customs declaration, and this value declaration is subject to be verified by competent customs officers.

#### Key Points
* Six sequential valuation methods applied in order: Transaction Value first, then identical goods, similar goods, induction, calculated, and last resort.
* Transaction Value used for >90% of trades; internationally encouraged by WTO and WCO.
* Traders may seek guidance on alternative methods from competent customs officers.

* In accordance with the existing regulations, customs value can be determined through these 06 methods:
    1. Transaction Value 
    2. Transaction Value of Identical Goods 
    3. Transaction Value of Similar Goods 
    4. Induction Value 
    5. Calculated Value 
    6. The Last Method.
* Customs value may be determined through any of the above 06 methods, but must be done in consequence from the first method: Transaction Value.
* Provided that the first method cannot be used, the second method shall be applied ; and if the second method cannot be applied, the third method shall be applied in such order, and that one method may not be skipped unless inapplicable.
* Based on international best practice, the first method (Transaction Value) is the most commonly used method for determining customs value (covering over 90% of the trades). Both the WTO and WCO strongly encouraged their members to use this method as extensively as possible before applying the following methods.
* In this regard, Cambodia customs also use Transaction Value method to determine​​ customs value.
* Aiming to improve the awareness and understanding of traders and the public regarding customs valuation, the GDCE published a short brochure explaining the application of the first method (Transaction Value).
* In case the first method is not applicable, related traders may seek advice about the application of other methods from competent customs officers.
* For exportation, the value used as the basis of calculation of export tariff is the value of the goods at the Cambodia’s border checkpoint of (Article 22, Law of Customs)

#### Key Points
* Customs valuation authority delegated to border checkpoints reduces clearance delays.
* Decentralization based on geographic location, consignment type, and trader compliance status.
* High-risk items and non-compliant traders handled at GDCE headquarter.

* Decentralization of customs valuation is the delegation of authority to make decision on customs value from the competent officers at the GDCE headquarter to the customs officers at the local customs checkpoint offices.
* This decentralization contributes to a more facilitative export-import procedure for traders by enabling them to directly get their consignments valued at the border checkpoints rather than the headquarter.
* As a result, the amount of time and cost of customs clearance is reduced.
* So far, decentralization of customs valuation has been made based on three risk criterion which are geographical location, types of consignment, and traders as follow:
    * Customs checkpoints bordering with Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, and at international airport 
    * General type of consignments, except for high-risk consignments such as motor vehicles, telecom equipment, petroleum products, beverages, gambling-related goods, and used goods etc.
    * High compliant traders as recognized by the GDCE. Among those are best traders who are not required to undergo customs valuation procedure during importation.

#### Key Points
* Non-commercial importations by state institutions and diplomatic missions are exempt from valuation.
* Humanitarian donations, samples, and personal effects skip valuation procedures.
* Best Traders and SEZ investors exempted from customs valuation verification.

* Certain types of consignment that fulfill the following criterion are not required to have their declared value verified by competent customs valuation officers:
    * a. Non-commercial importations by legal entities such as embassies, state institutions, and other organization where tax and duty are to be made as state burden 
    * b. Other non-commercial importations as humanitarian donation, personal use, sample, exhibition good to be re-exported, personal effect for residential moving, and low-value importations of border-crossing passengers and near-border residents.
    * c. Importation consignments of best traders and investors at Special Economic Zone.

### Customs Valuation Procedure
* **A. Location:**
    * Customs valuation units at customs and excise branches and offices (under the decentralized scope) 
    * Department of Planning and Technique at the GDCE Headquarter 
* **B. Documents required for customs valuation:**
    * To have their consignment valued by customs officers, traders shall lodge a Customs Valuation Declaration and attach the following documents in electronic form through the Customs Valuation Declaration System (CVDS) at http://value.customskh.com/cv/:
        * Commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading 
        * VAT certificate, patent certificate, letter of authorization, identification document (ID Card, Passport) of the importer and representative 
        * Import permit (if applicable) 
    * Under some circumstances, competent customs officers may require that the traders supply additional supporting documents such as:
        * Sale contract, purchase order, letter of credit, public price list, and other documents related to the sale or transaction 
        * Documents detailing the information of the goods 
* **C. Correct and valid documents are:**
    * Duly completed in every required field 
    * Without irregularity or tampering 
    * Certified copy (through the company’s stamp) for photocopied documents etc.
* **D. Eligible individuals:**
    * Importing company’s owner or 
    * Importing company’s employee authorized by the owner (company’s ID card is required) 
    * Legal person or physical person with legal status as a customs broker 
* **E. Duration of the customs valuation procedure:**
    * Provided that the submitted documents are complete and correct, decision on customs valuation can be made within one or two working days at the latest.
    * In case this could not be done due to unforeseeable circumstance, competent customs officers will provide a remark on the relevant documents providing reasons for this delay.
* **F. Appeal procedures regarding customs valuation:**
    * Individuals who are not satisfied with the decision made by the competent customs officers can submit a written appeal to the GDCE in accordance with Article 24 of the Law on Customs.
* **G. Communication channel:**
    * In case there’s query regarding the customs valuation methods or customs valuation procedures, related individual can seek out further clarification at the Department of Planning and Technique at the GDCE.

#### Key Points
* Prohibited and restricted goods protect national security, public order, health, and natural resources.
* Anukret 370 (2023) defines 5 annexes: Prohibited, Restricted, Export Certificate, Transit, and Explanatory notes.
* Tariff lines and competent authorities specified for each prohibited/restricted item.

* Prohibited and restricted goods refer to goods that are banned or are subject to fulfill import, export, or international transit through Cambodia due to the following reasons:
    * Protection of national security 
    * Protection of public order, ethical, or moral value 
    * Protection of humans, animals, or botanical health or welfare 
    * Protection of national heritage of artistic, historic or anthropological value 
    * Conservation of natural resources 
    * Stipulation in existing laws and regulations 
    * Requirement in United Nations Conventions 
* Article 8 of the Laws of Customs enables the Royal Government of Cambodia to issue an Anukret determining goods to be considered prohibited or restricted.
* In accordance with the abovementioned reasons, the Royal Government of Cambodia issued and has subsequently amended the Anukret on the Promulgation of the List of Prohibited and Restricted Goods.
* This list defined the tariff lines and competent government authorities who issue Permit or similar document for the export or import of such goods.
* The amendments have been done in order to increase effectiveness of the management of risks that could harm the well-being of human, animals, and the environment.
* Factors taken into account are development of socio-economy, emergence of new items and disappearance of certain items, necessity for trade facilitation, and the government policies etc. As of 2024, this Anukret has been amended thrice:
    * The Anukret 209 dated 31st December 2007 
    * The Anukret 17 dated 26th February 2020 
    * The Anukret 370 dated 28th December 2023 consisting of 05 main annexes:
        * **Annex 1 – List of Prohibited Goods:** Goods that are prohibited from exportation, importation or international transit through Cambodia’s territory unless permitted by the Royal Government of Cambodia.
        * **Annex 2 – List of Restricted Goods:** Goods that are required to have export or import permit or similar document issued by competent government ministries/agencies prior to the exportation or importation.
        * **Annex 3 – List of Goods to be accompanied with export certificate:** Goods that are not required to obtain prior import permit in the case of importation in Cambodia, but they are required to obtain export certificate or similar document issued by competent authority in the exporting country.
        * **Annex 4 – List of Goods Restricted for International Transit:** Goods that are required to obtain prior transit permit from competent government ministries/agencies.
        * **Annex 5 – Explanatory Note:** which provides explanation on how the list could be read, definition of certain keywords, and some other additional notes on goods that could not be technically classified based on the AHTN, yet are also subject to restriction or prohibition, and such.

#### Key Points
* Other procedures cover postal goods, passenger effects, non-commercial goods, and special situations.
* Streamlined processes for low-value items, humanitarian goods, and travel-related shipments.
* Specialized procedures for de minimis goods, currencies, and human remains.

#### Key Points
* Single Administration Document (SAD) for commercial imports over 300 USD; Summary Declaration for non-commercial.
* De Minimis rule exempts FOB value ≤ 50 USD from duties and taxes if not prohibited goods.
* Customs officials may allow parcel opening before declaration if contents unknown.

* Goods imported through courier service or through postal service are to be reported by the exporter of the consignment. 
* The owner or the representative in Cambodia must complete customs declaration manually or electronically and must attach supporting documents including invoice, packing list, and transport document. 
* If deemed necessary by customs, the owner or the representative is required to submit other supporting documents such as manifest, import/export permit, certificate of origin, certificate of insurance, etc. 
* There are two types of customs declaration: 
    * Single Administration Document (SAD) which is to be completed in ASYCUDA (for commercial import or consignment valued over the equivalence of 300 USD);  and 
    * Summary Declaration which is to be completed in E-Customs (for non-commercial import or consignment valued not over the equivalence of 300 USD). 
* In case the owner or the legal representative does not have any information regarding the nature of the item in the parcel or container, customs official may allow the owner or the legal representative to open the parcel before making the declaration. 
* The opening of the parcel is to be carried out in the presence of customs official and postal official. 
* The importer or the legal representative must declare the transaction value (price actually paid or payable) in accordance with Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 of Prakas no. 
* 387 MEF.GDCE dated 22 May 2008 of the Ministry of Economy and Finance on Customs Valuation on Imported Goods and must present other documentary proofs including invoice(s) and other relevant documents. 
* Competent customs official will verify the declared customs value. In case there is any irregularity or uncertainty, the owner is required to present additional proofs to prove the authenticity and correctness of the declared value. 
* In case the owner or the legal representative is not able to declare the value of the goods due to the absence of sale or due to the inapplicability of the declared transaction value, customs value will be determined based on other rules in accordance with existing customs law and regulations. 
* Competent customs official will inspect the consignment and verify with the information declared on form(s) of Universal Postal Union (UPU) (also known as CN22/CN23 which is sticked onto the parcel by foreign postal official/agent) 
* After having inspected the parcel, customs official will finalize the customs formalities by allowing the owner to pay duty and tax in accordance with existing law and regulations.

#### Key Points
* Express parcels with FOB value ≤ 50 USD receive duty/tax exemption.
* De Minimis rule does not apply to prohibited goods or public security-sensitive items.
* Goods containing weapons, explosives, drugs, or military equipment cannot qualify for exemption.

* In case the postal good is in form of express parcel that is of non-commercial nature and/or of similar form, of which the FOB value is equivalent to 50 USD or below, the tax and duty on the good will be exempted. 
* De Minimis rule is not applicable to the following items: 
    * Goods that are registered in the list of prohibited and restricted goods in accordance with Anukret 17 ANK.BK dated 26 February 2020. 
    * Other goods with high sensitivity to public security and safety such as weapons, explosives, military equipment, drugs and precursors, and other dangerous materials/substances.

#### Key Points
* Customs officials complete formalities for postal officials on all exported parcels.
* Three CN forms retained: CN38 (air dispatch), CN37 (land/sea), CN33 (special mail).
* Customs retains one copy of each accompanying document form.

1. Customs officials shall complete formalities for postal officials regarding exporting mail parcels. 
2. After completion, customs officials shall retain one copy of the following forms: 
    * CN38: accompanying document for parcel dispatched via air. 
    * CN37: accompanying document for parcel dispatched via land, rail, or sea. 
    * CN33: document listing parcel dispatched via special mail.

#### Key Points
* Customs officials have right to enter postal office sites for international parcel inspection.
* Inspections conducted in presence of postal official per Universal Postal Union facilitation.
* Postcards, printed materials, transit parcels, and diplomatic mail exempt from physical inspection.

* Customs officials have the rights to enter any site of the postal office where the dispatch of international postal parcels takes place in order to inspect, in the presence of postal official, postal parcels with domestic and foreign origin containing goods or that are believed to contain goods in accordance with the provisions set out in Universal Postal Convention. 
* In accordance with the Universal Postal Convention and Universal Postal Union’s facilitation, postal authority shall provide facilitation to customs administration in their inspection of postal parcels that are subject to customs duty and tax, to customs inspection, or to other restriction or prohibition. 
* Customs inspection of postal mail shall be carried out in the presence of postal official or the owner of the mail (article 16). 
* Physical inspection may be exempted for the following types of postal parcel: 
    * Postcards and letters containing purely personal messages or braille 
    * Printed materials not subject to duty and tax. 
    * Postal parcels under international transit. 
    * Postal parcels of foreign consular or diplomatic mission or official delegations of foreign government.

### Importation of non-commercial goods
* Non-commercial goods are goods occasionally imported by traveler or by resident at the border for their personal use or using at the border area. 
* Importation of non-commercial goods shall be implemented as follows: 
    * An occasionally importation of goods by passenger deemed as non-commercial is subject to fulfillment of customs procedures in accordance with law in force and require importer to show a passport that certifies the entry to and exit from the country from competent authorities at check point. 
    * Customs receipt shall be stamped or written "non-commercial - for personal use". No use customs seal is required. 
    * In case of passenger occasionally imports of goods for commercial purpose, customs value shall twenty (20) percent added on the existing customs valuation and stamped or written "for commercial” on the customs receipt, sealed if the goods is under Customs seal systems to be circulated on the market. 
    * Importation of resident at the border area is subject to fulfillment of customs procedures in accordance with law in force. 
    * Customs receipt shall be stamped or written "For circulation in the border area”. 
    * The resident at the border area who performs commercial export and import transactions throughout the country set up a company with VAT identification number and patent as normally importer-exporter and if necessary shall follow the instructions above.

#### Key Points
* De Minimis goods (express parcels, FOB value ≤ 50 USD) exempt from customs duty and taxes.
* Summary declaration and supporting documents required for administrative tracking.
* Prohibited goods and security-sensitive items excluded from De Minimis exemption.

* Goods exported or imported under De Minimis procedure is referred to goods in the form of express parcel, non-commercial goods, or goods in similar form and has FOB value no greater than USD 50. 
* To facilitate trade following international best practice, the export or import of De Minimis is not obliged to pay customs duty. 
* Nevertheless, the owner or his/her representative shall follow a simple procedure by lodging a summary customs declaration and attaching supporting documents such as invoice, packing list, certificate of tax registration, airway bill/bill of lading, and other relevant documents if available. 
* Some risky commodities, however, are not considered as “De Minimis”. These commodities include: 
    * absolutely prohibited goods for export/import which are on the list of prohibited and restricted goods of the current law and regulations. 
    * highly sensitive goods that may potentially affect public security and safety such as weapons, explosives, military equipment, drug, drug pre-cursor, and other hazardous substances.

* No limit on currency quantity; amounts <10,000 USD do not require customs declaration.

* To ensure a smooth travel across the border of any passengers coming in and going out of Cambodia, who wish to bring currencies​ or bank notes with them, it is crucial for them to know Customs Procedure to export and import foreign currencies. 
* Currency refers to payment instruments or securities denominated in foreign currency, raw gold, raw precious metals, or uncut precious stones. 
* There is no limit on the quantity of currencies or bank notes exported/imported from/to Cambodia by any delegates, passengers, or other natural persons or legal persons; 
* however, the import maybe subjected to customs declaration. The procedure to export/import currencies or bank notes is described below:

#### Key Points
* Currencies <10,000 USD do not require declaration; amounts ≥10,000 USD must be declared at checkpoint.
* Intermediary banks export currencies with National Bank permit; private persons use checkpoint declaration.
* Raw precious metals/stones ≥10,000 USD equivalent require dual National Bank and customs declaration.

1. To export or import currencies less than 10,000 USD, a passenger is not required to complete a customs declaration. 
2. A traveler who exports or imports Cambodian currency or foreign currencies equivalent to 10,000 USD or more shall lodge customs declaration at the border checkpoint. 
3. The export of foreign currencies in cash by intermediary banks (the banks situate in Cambodia) needs to submit a declaration at the National Bank in advance. 
4. The export or import of raw gold, uncut precious stone, or raw precious metal having equivalent value to USD 10,000 or more shall require lodgment of a declaration at the National Bank and a customs declaration at the border checkpoint of Cambodia. 
5. The exporter or importer of currencies or bank notes that are subjected to customs declaration shall: 
    * fill in the declaration with correct, sufficient, and clear information on type and quantity of the currencies or bank notes that are carried along or sent via another person or air parcel. 
    * travel through the assigned checkpoint and show the currencies or bank notes to the customs officers 
    * be a representative of the intermediary bank, and show the customs officers the export permit from the National Bank, the permit from customs administration, invoice and packing list and transportation document, and etc.

#### Key Points
* Foreign corpse exportation requires Ministry of Foreign Affairs permission and police/hospital death certification.

* It is noticed so far that there are requests to export or import human corpse by those whose family member or relative passing away in a foreign country for a funeral following the tradition, custom, and culture in their home country. 
* In this regard, to facilitate the process, the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia creates this webpage to provide information regarding customs procedure for the export or import of human corpse.

### Exporting human corpse of a foreigner from Cambodia 
1. A person who wishes to export the remain of his/her foreign family member or friend, deceased in Cambodia because of disease or other accidents, shall: 
    * request permission from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Kingdom of Cambodia. 
    * fill in the Summary Declaration in e-Customs system with the following necessary attached document៖ 
        * Permission from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (Sample Document) 
        * Death Certification issued by the police 
        * Death Certification issued by hospital (Sample Document) 
        * Quarantine permit for exportation of corpse (Sample Document) 
        * Transportation document (Sample Document) 
    * invite customs officers for on-site inspection in order to make inspection note before placing the corpse into the casket for export.

### Importing a Cambodian human remain from abroad 
* A person who wishes to import the remain of his/her Cambodian family member or friend, deceased abroad, back to Cambodia for a traditional funeral shall: 
    * fill in the Summary Declaration in e-Customs system at the entrance checkpoint and attach the following necessary document៖ 
        * Letter of the Embassy of Kingdom of Cambodia based in that country (Sample Document) 
        * Death Certification issued by authority of the export country 
        * Death Certification issued by hospital (Sample Document) 
        * Transportation document (Sample Document)

### Exporting and Importing casket 
* The export or import of casket(s) containing human corpse(s) is not subject to customs duty and tax. 
* However, an empty casket (without human corpse) is considered as a goods and is obliged to pay customs duty according to current Customs Tariff of Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* Customs administration can settle monetary fines only before court decision.
* Office chiefs settle offenses ≤1.5M KHR; branch chiefs/directors settle ≤4M KHR; DG has unlimited authority.
* Offenders must request settlement within 30 days; 90-day unresolved cases referred to court.

* In accordance with Article 77 of the Law of Customs, Customs administration has the right to settle customs offences. 
* This right of settlement applies only to monetary fines. The settlement shall occur only before any decision by competent court has been made.

### Customs’ rights of settlement: 
* Chiefs of Customs Office have the right to settle all types of customs offences in relation to goods valued not more than one million five hundred thousand (1,500,000) KHR. 
* Chief of Customs Branch or Directors of Department have the right to settle all types of customs offences in relation to goods valued not more than four million (4,000,000) KHR. 
* The Director General of Customs has the right to settle all types of customs offences.

### Customs Offences Settlement Procedures: 
* Within thirty (30) days from the date of the customs offence record or other customs record, individual subject to the customs record is required to request for settlement if he/she wishes to settle the offence without having to proceed the case to competent court. 
* This right to settlement and the time limit shall be stated in the customs record. 
* If within 90 days from the date of the customs offence records or other customs records, no official decision regarding the settlement has been made, the case shall be referred to competent court. 
* The related individual must comply with the term and provision set out in the official decision on the settlement of customs offence including the penalty, fine, tax, duty, and other obligation set out in the official decision within ninety (90) days from the date of the decision. 
* If the related individual failed to comply with the decision within the timeframe set out, the goods subject to the decision will be considered as unclaimed good in accordance with article 54 and article 55 of the law of customs.

* Individual may lodge the appeal at Customs units as follow:

* Otherwise, the appeal application is considered to be agreed. 
* If the concerned individual is not satisfied with decision of the GDCE, the individual has the right to appeal to other competent institutions including the court of justice. 
* The appeal has to be filed within 30 days after receiving the decision of the GDCE.

#### Key Points
* Tariff classification, origin, or customs value can be re-determined by customs within 3 years post-declaration.
* Written appeal to GDCE within 30 days of re-determination notice; GDCE responds within 60 days.
* Importer can appeal GDCE decision to Fiscal Dispute Resolution Committee, then to court within 30 days.

* Individual, importer, or his/her agent, who completes a Customs declaration must declare the tariff classification, origin, and customs value of goods for duty and tax calculation (Article 18 of Customs Laws). 
* Within 3 years from the date of registration of Customs declaration, following audit, investigation, inspection, or examination of the imported goods, Customs may re-determine the declared tariff classification, origin, or customs value by issuing a notice stating the reason for this re-determination.  (Article 18 of Customs Laws) 
* In case where the individual, importer, or his/her agent is not satisfied with the new Customs assessment on tariff classification, origin, or custom valuation in the notice above, they may make a written appeal to the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia (GDCE) within 30 days from the date of receipt of the Customs notice. 
* The GDCE must respond within 60 days after receiving the written appeal. (Article 24 of Customs Laws) 
* Importer or his/her agents who objects to the above decision of the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia may appeal in writing to the Fiscal Dispute Resolution Committee.  (Article 24 of the Law on Customs) 
* Individual, importer, or his/her agent who objects the decision from the Fiscal Dispute Resolution Committee has the right to appeal to the competent court within thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of the notice of the Fiscal Dispute Resolution Committee.  (Article 24 of Customs Laws)

* The mechanism was officially launched on 26 January 2010 to further enhance fair business and investment climate. 
* The main mission of the CPPM is to facilitate cooperation and mutual understanding between the Customs Administration and the private sector in order to resolve all customs-related issues to the fullest extent possible before proceeding to resolve at inter-ministerial level or submitted to the Royal Government Forum- Private Sector. 
* The result of this mutually beneficial cooperation has become an important part of ensuring the effective implementation of the Royal Government of Cambodia's trade facilitation policy and contributing to the promotion of an equitable and competitive business environment.  Cambodia.

#### Key Points
* TRS measures effectiveness of customs clearance time from cargo arrival to physical release.
* 2013 TRS: Average turnaround ~2d 14h 39m; customs-only clearance ~1h 57m.
* 2019 TRS: Full process ~3d 13h 11m (1 day longer); customs clearance improved to ~1h 5m.

* The Time Release Study (TRS) is a special tool developed by the World Customs Organization (WCO) to measure the relevant aspects of the effectiveness of operational procedures carried out by Customs, other regulatory agencies and private sector stakeholders in the standard processing of imports, exports, cross border and transit movements. 
* The aim of the TRS is to find out the average time taken for the clearance of consignments from the arrival until the physical release of cargo and to prescribe possible corrective measures to the Customs and other border agencies to improve their performance.

### The Time Release Study in Cambodia 2013 
* In 2013 the General Department of Customs and Excise of Cambodia (GDCE) in collaboration with Asian Development Bank (ADB), WCO and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) undertook its first TRS based on the WCO TRS Guide. 
* The 2013 TRS survey measured the customs clearance time from the arrival of the goods to the removal of the goods from the customs, but it did not count the time taken to request for license or permits. 
* The results of the 2013 TRS survey has identified areas that need to be addressed to reduce or eliminate bottlenecks in order to improve the trade facilitation in Cambodia. 
* To address the bottlenecks found in the 2013 TRS survey, the GDCE has embarked on customs reform and modernization aiming at the improvement of many things from organizational structure, human development to customs policies to the application of Information and Communications Technology (ICT) initiatives in customs works. 
* The results of the study found the average time taken as follow: 
    * Cargo arrival to removal from customs control (turnaround time) is 2d 14h 39m. 
    * SAD Lodgment - Removal from customs control is 0d 5h 37m. 
    * SAD Lodgment - Cargo Release Note (customs only) is 0d 1h 57m.

### The Time Release Study in Cambodia 2019 
* The TRS 2019 survey is extended not only to measure the customs clearance time from the arrival of the goods to the removal of the goods, but also to cover the pre-arrival process procedure by measuring time taken to request for license or permits conducted by Customs and other relevant government agencies. 
* The expansion of scope of the 2nd TRS was made to align with ASEAN minimum requirements and its outcome would be used as a proxy to calculate the reduction of Trade Transaction Cost (TTC) within ASEAN.

**Major Findings** 
* The 2019 TRS shows that the whole clearance process from the arrival of cargo until its physical release from the ports/checkpoints takes averagely 3d 13h 11 m, which is one day longer than that of the 2013 TRS. 
* However, the customs clearance time in 2019 has dropped averagely 50 minutes, which is down from 1h 57m to 1h 5m.

    * **Customs Valuation Verification:**  The process of complete Customs Valuation Verification is under responsibility of Department of Planning and Technique of GDCE.  It takes an average of 0d 5h 48m to complete this process.

    * **Ministry of Agriculture Forestry and Fishery (MAFF):**  The process of issuing license or permit at MAFF takes an average of 4d 22h 8m to complete.

#### Key Points
* Cambodia National Single Window provides online services for faster, transparent export-import procedures.
* Enables G2G, G2B, and B2B cooperation for reducing costs and improving consistency.
* Connected to ASEAN Single Window for Certificate of Origin exchange; Phase 3 implementation ongoing.

* The Cambodia National Single Window has been developed to provide electronic services (online) to facilitate faster and more transparent export-import procedures, reduce costs, provide consistency and reliability for proceedings from the start of the required procedures to the completion of customs clearance. 
* The most important goal of The Cambodia National Single Window is to strengthen cooperation between government-to-government (G2G), government-to-business (G2B) and business-to-business (B2B). 
* The Royal Government of Cambodia has announced its commitment to develop Cambodia National Single Window to support trade facilitation policies in line with international agreements and international best practices, especially with ASEAN and the World Trade Organization (WTO). 
* The Cambodia National Single Window has been launched for the application of permits, licenses, certificates and other documents (LPCO) required for export and import issued by major ministries/institutions, namely; 
    * the Ministry of Commerce, the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, the Council for the Development of Cambodia and the General Department of Customs​ and Excises. 
* At the same time, the Cambodia National Single Window is also connected to the ASEAN Single Window for the electronic exchange of the Certificate of Origin (ATIGA e-Form D), the ASEAN Customs Declaration Document (ACDD) and other international trade-related documents with ASEAN members and ASEAN dialog partners. 
* Currently, Cambodia National Single Window project is in the stage of the implementation of phase 3 which including all ministries and institutions involved in the issuance of permits, licenses, certificates and other documents, namely; 
    * Ministry of Economy and Finance, Ministry Environment, Ministry of National Defense, Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts, Ministry of Mines and Energy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, Commercial Gambling Management Commission of Cambodia and National Bank of Cambodia.

# Customs FAQs

---

## Customs Declaration and Clearance

### How must a customs declaration be completed?

* The customs declaration, also known as the **Single Administrative Document (SAD)**, is a unified document used for all customs clearance procedures, including:  
  * Import  
  * Export  
  * Customs warehousing
* The declaration must comply with **Prakas No. 3447 MEF dated 26 December 2007**, and all fields must be correctly filled according to regulations.

#### Key Points
* SAD is the official document for all customs clearance procedures.  
* Must comply with Prakas No. 3447 MEF.  
* Fields must be filled accurately according to regulations.

---

* A transportation document is required in the following cases:  
  * When imported goods cannot be transported in a single trip due to quantity or logistical reasons  
  * When goods are transported with a tax invoice and verified identification  
  * For legal transportation with proper licenses or Ministry approvals
* Each transportation document must be accompanied by a **confirmation note “Seen Through”** from Customs and Excise Units along the route.

#### Key Points
* Required for multi-trip, licensed, or verified shipments.  
* Must include “Seen Through” confirmation from customs units.

---

* Taxes and tariffs on imported and exported goods follow a sequential calculation:  
  * **Import Tax (COP)**  
  * **Special Tariff (SOP)**, if applicable  
  * **VAT (VOP)**

#### Key Points
* Tax calculation is sequential: Import Tax → Special Tariff → VAT.  
* Formulas vary depending on goods type.

---

#### Import Tax (COP)

* **Formula:**  
  * Import Tax (COP) = Customs Value × Import Tax Rate

#### Key Points
* Import Tax calculated as Customs Value × Import Tax Rate.

---

#### Special Tariff (SOP)

* **Formula:**  
  * Special Tariff (SOP) = (Customs Value + Import Tax) × Special Tariff Rate

#### Key Points
* SOP is applied on Customs Value + Import Tax, using Special Tariff Rate.

---

#### VAT (VOP)

* **Formula for non-taxable goods:**  
  * VOP = (Customs Value + Import Tax) × 10%

* **Formula for general taxable goods:**  
  * VOP = (Customs Value + Import Tax + Special Tariff) × 10%

#### Key Points
* VAT is 10% applied sequentially depending on taxable goods.

---

#### Example Calculation

* Company A imports 20 cases of beer.

* **Customs Value:** 4,000,000 Riels  
* **Rates:**  
  * Import Tax: 35%  
  * Special Tariff: 25%  
  * VAT: 10%

#### Key Points
* Demonstrates sequential calculation of duties and taxes.  
* Total duties = Import Tax + Special Tariff + VAT.

---

* A guarantee can take the form of:  
  * Cash or certified cheque  
  * Bond or security from an approved surety (bank, insurance, or government)  
  * Other forms approved by the Director of Customs

* Guarantees are required for:  
  * Clearance of goods before payment  
  * Transit movements within customs territory  
  * Bonded warehouse or temporary storage operations  
  * Temporary import/export  
  * Release of goods pending appeals or seizures

#### Key Points
* Guarantees ensure duties/taxes are secured.  
* Can be cash, bond, or other approved forms.  
* Required in specific customs operations.

---

## Goods Storage and Handling

### What are unclaimed goods?

* Unclaimed goods include:  
  * Goods exceeding temporary storage timeframes  
  * Goods sent by post but refused or cannot be returned

#### Key Points
* Goods not collected within timeframes or refused are considered unclaimed.

---

* Authorized containers must:  
  * Be sealable/rigid with multiple stamping points  
  * Allow one-time or multiple transport without transferring goods  
  * Facilitate loading/unloading  
  * Meet verified dimensions: 20 ft × 40 ft × 45 ft

#### Key Points
* Containers must be secure, compliant with dimensions, and suitable for transport.

---

* Goods prohibited under transit include:  
  * Restricted items by Sub-decree 209 (31 Dec 2007)  
  * Socially dangerous items: weapons, drugs, hazardous materials  
  * Items prohibited internationally: endangered species, antiques, nuclear elements

#### Key Points
* Certain restricted, dangerous, or internationally prohibited goods cannot transit.

---

* Procedures:  
  * Transportation must be accompanied by a factory letter specifying invoice/warehouse token, product specs, quantity, route, departure/destination, verification date  
  * Factory is responsible for fraudulent acts or non-compliance

#### Key Points
* Factory provides documentation and ensures compliance.  
* Customs verifies product details before export.

---

* Permitted checkpoints:  
  * Bavet, Svay Reang Province  
  * Trapang Plong, Kampong Cham Province (Tbong Khmum)  
  * Trapang Sre, Kratie Province  
  * Poi Pet, Banteay Meanchey Province  
  * Chamyeam, Koh Kong Province  
  * Duong, Battambong Province (temporary)  
  * Trapang Kreal, Steoung Treng Province (temporary)

#### Key Points
* Only listed checkpoints allow third-country containers under transit regime.

---

* Penalized individuals can submit a **written complaint** to GDCE within **30 days** after confiscation, including:  
  * Name, address, signature  
  * Confiscation record details (with copies)

#### Key Points
* Complaints must be submitted in writing within 30 days.  
* Include identity and confiscation details.

---
* If GDCE fails to resolve, the complainant may escalate to **competent authorities or juridical bodies** after 30 days from Director of Customs’ settlement.

#### Key Points
* Complaints unresolved by GDCE may escalate after 30 days.  
* Escalation follows legal or judicial procedures.
